findings.title: Hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip shows the uncapped total, so it disagrees with the Breakdown and with Gross − Take-home whenever flat deductions exceed gross
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3487 (chip reads calc.ded); computeNet 1231-1255 (ded uncapped, pre/post capped for display, flat-dollar custom withholdings never capped); Breakdown 3980-3987
findings.detail: computeNet returns `ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw` (raw) alongside display-capped `pre`/`post`. The hero chip prints `ded`; the Breakdown prints the capped rows. The skill's own invariant says the caps exist 'so Breakdown still sums' — but the hero never received the same treatment, and the flat-dollar half of `cw` is outside the cap too (line 1243 folds dollar and percent withholdings into one number, line 1247 caps only pretax/posttax). Any nurse whose pretax/posttax fields are non-zero — which a paystub scan sets automatically (applyPaystub 3376-3378) — sees this on every pay period that is empty or light.
findings.failure: pretax $600 + posttax $25 (typical after a paystub scan), scroll to next pay period with no shifts logged yet: hero reads 'Gross $0 · Taxes & deductions –$625 · $0'. Log one 8h base shift at the default $65.15: hero reads 'Gross $521 · Taxes & deductions –$665 · $0' while 'See the full breakdown' for the same period lists Pre-tax –$481 and FICA –$40, total –$521. Same shape with a flat-dollar custom withholding: $150 'Parking' on an empty period shows 'Other withholdings –$150' under 'Gross $0'.
findings.fix: Have computeNet return a display total that is bounded by gross (e.g. `dedDisp = Math.min(ded, gross)` or literally `gross - net`) and print that in the hero chip; extend the flat cap to the dollar-typed custom withholdings (track `cwFlat` separately from `cwPct` and apply the same `flatCapTotal` logic) so the Breakdown's 'Other withholdings' row is bounded too. Add a smoke probe: computeNet(0,{pretax:600}).dedDisp === 0 and Breakdown rows sum === gross − net when pretax > gross.

findings.title: A blanked or garbage multiplier differential is coerced to 0×, silently pricing every shift of that type at $0
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1046-1047 (sanitizeData: `amount: isFinite(amt) ? amt : 0` regardless of type); 4715 (Settings multiplier NumInput with min={0}); 4016-4023 (NumInput commits `min` on an empty field); 1121 (hourlyRate: `base * diff.amount`)
findings.detail: For a dollar-type differential, 0 is the neutral value. For a multiplier-type differential (Holiday 1.5×, Overtime 1.5×), 0 zeroes the entire hourly rate — `hourlyRate` returns base*0 and shiftGross returns only the per-hour/flat bonus. Two paths produce it: NumInput's blank→min contract commits 0 when the user clears the '×' field and blurs, and sanitizeData maps any non-finite blob value to 0 rather than to 1. Once written, 0 is a finite number so sanitizeData keeps it on every subsequent load; nothing ever repairs it.
findings.failure: In Settings, tap the Holiday '1.5 ×' field, select-all/delete to retype, then tap elsewhere before typing (common on a phone). Holiday becomes 0×. Her Christmas 12h shift now shows '~$0' on the calendar and the hero's projected take-home drops by roughly $913 (65.15×1.5×12×0.78) with no warning; the Settings row still reads '0 ×' and looks like a value she chose.
findings.fix: In sanitizeData's differential branch, when `type==='multiplier'` coerce non-finite or ≤0 amounts to 1 (not 0). In the Settings row, give multiplier NumInputs `min={0.1}` (or make NumInput's empty-commit revert to the last good value when a `revertOnBlank` prop is set). Add a probe: sanitizeData({differentials:{holiday:{type:'multiplier',amount:''}}}).differentials.holiday.amount === 1 and hourlyRate(50,{type:'multiplier',amount:0}) is never reached from a sanitized blob.

findings.title: Independently rounded chips: Gross − Taxes ≠ Take-home by $1 in ~11% of pay periods; Breakdown rows drift the same way
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3484-3487 (hero: fmt(calc.net), fmt(calc.gross), fmt(calc.ded) each rounded separately); 3982-3987 and 4006 (Breakdown: six rows and the take-home each rounded separately); fmt at 1116
findings.detail: `fmt` rounds each figure to whole dollars on its own, so the three hero chips are three independent roundings of gross, ded and gross−ded. Replaying the real shiftGross/computeNet formulas over 220 mixes of base/night 12h shifts at five base rates with default taxes, 24 (11%) print chips whose subtraction is off by one. With six Breakdown rows the residual can reach $3. This is the 'rounding that compounds' the lens asks about — small, but it is the arithmetic a nurse is most likely to check by hand, and the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing.
findings.failure: Two 12h base shifts at the default $65.15/hr, default taxes: hero prints 'Gross $1,564 · Taxes & deductions –$346' over a take-home of '$1,217'. 1,564 − 346 = 1,218.
findings.fix: Display-only: derive the chip as `Math.round(calc.gross) - Math.round(calc.net)` (and likewise give Breakdown the rounding residual on its largest row, or print cents), so the visible figures always close. No change to net/gross/ded themselves — but it changes displayed dollar text, so run the wage-core equality assertion and name this as the one intended difference.

findings.title: Pattern lab and calendar price a toggled-off differential differently
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1206-1213 (patternCellShiftType resolves a 'night'/weekend cell to 'base' unless differentials[k].active); 2646 (statOf) and 2795 (calc) call shiftGross(baseRate, differentials[s.shiftType], s) with no active check; hourlyRate 1119-1124
findings.detail: The Settings toggle dims the row and removes the chip from the Add-Shift sheet (4099), and the lab treats it as 'she doesn't get this differential' — but calc/statOf/yearMonths keep applying the amount to any shift already carrying that shiftType (logged before the toggle, imported from .ics via the questionnaire at 3184, or added by a template/quick-fill). Only the delete path (4691) warns about repricing, which implies toggling off was meant to be display-only; the lab contradicts that. Either semantics is defensible; the two surfaces holding different ones is the defect.
findings.failure: Log Mon–Wed 12h nights this period (or .ics-import them), then toggle Night off in Settings. Hero still prices them at $75.15/hr (night amount included, +$360 gross for the period). Open Patterns → 'Mon–Wed nights' preset anchored on the same week: it prices the identical three nights at $65.15/hr and shows a take-home per paycheck ~$280 lower than the hero for the same schedule.
findings.fix: Pick one: (a) make hourlyRate/shiftGross treat `diff.active===false` as no differential so the calendar reprices to match the lab and the dimmed row (then the delete warning applies to toggling too, and the Settings hint should say so); or (b) drop the `active()` gate in patternCellShiftType so the lab prices what the calendar prices. (a) touches wage core; (b) does not, but leaves the toggle as pure decluttering. Either way add a probe covering an inactive differential on both paths.

findings.title: Every '~take-home' preview ignores percent custom withholdings that computeNet deducts (and sampleNet re-implements the tax model without them)
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio = 1 − (federal+state+FICA)/100 only); computeNet 1243 (percent customWithholdings taken from every marginal dollar); consumers: 4105/4245-4248 (Add-Shift preview, ≈$/hr, goal %), 3919/3933 (calendar cells), 3434/3512 (weekend-night nudge), 4747 (Settings goal reverse); sampleNet 3416-3424
findings.detail: A percent-typed custom withholding is a marginal deduction exactly like state tax, so a preview built from keepRatio overstates the marginal take-home of a shift by that percentage relative to the hero it is meant to foreshadow. sampleNet (onboarding step 4) is a second hand-rolled copy of computeNet that also omits customWithholdings. Exposure is limited: there is no Settings editor for customWithholdings today (only the Breakdown row reads them), so they only arrive via Import JSON or a legacy blob — which is why this is low, not medium. The #65 harness deliberately covered percent+dollar withholdings, so the owner treats them as live data.
findings.failure: Blob carries customWithholdings:[{name:'401k',amount:6,type:'percent'}]. The Add-Shift preview for a 12h night at $65.15 says 'about +$702 take-home' and '≈$58.50/hr'; saving it moves the hero by $648 (≈$54/hr). Every calendar cell and the 'Pick up a weekend night? about +$X' card overstate by the same 6%.
findings.fix: Add the sum of percent-typed customWithholdings amounts to the keepRatio subtraction (one line at 2820) and make sampleNet call computeNet(gross, taxInputs) instead of its own copy. Both change displayed dollars, so run the equality assertion with a percent withholding seeded and name the intended difference.

findings.title: Year view prints gross as a bare '$' figure while the month cells it opens into print estimated take-home
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3971 (YearList: fmt(mm.g), no qualifier); 2769-2780 (yearMonths sums shiftGross + PTO gross); 3933 and 3580 (month cells print '~'+fmt(t.g*keepRatio) under the disclaimer 'Day amounts are estimated take-home')
findings.detail: The month view carries a disclaimer that day amounts are take-home; the Year list has no equivalent and shows gross with the same `$` formatting. Tapping a year row drops the user into that month, so the two figures are seen back to back for the same days.
findings.failure: Year view shows 'September · 72 hrs · $5,327 · 6 shifts'. Tap it: the six day cells inside read ~$702, ~$702, ~$702, ~$716, ~$716, ~$609 — about $4,147 total, 22% less than the row she just tapped, with nothing on either screen explaining that one is gross and the other is take-home.
findings.fix: Display-only: either label the year row ('$5,327 gross') or print `'~'+fmt(mm.g*keepRatio)` to match the cells and reuse the same disclaimer. No math change.

findings.title: Paystub import turns a premium-only earnings row into a negative differential
findings.where: index.html:3386-3387 (applyPaystub) and index.html:3739-3745 (PaystubReview row rendering)
findings.detail: applyPaystub derives each differential as `da = round((s.rate - p.baseRate)*100)/100` and stores it as the dollar amount with no floor and no cross-check against `s.earnings`. The parser's row regex (index.html:3360-3363) captures the HOURS AND EARNINGS 'Rate' column as `s.rate`. On PeopleSoft-style stubs (the very format this parser targets: 'Fed MED/EE', 'Fed OASDI/EE', 'TOTAL GROSS'), a shift-differential earnings code is frequently listed at the premium rate alone (e.g. 'PD Night Diff  4.00  36.00  144.00'), not the base-plus-premium rate. The review sheet renders the same `da` via `+$${da.toFixed(2)}/hr` with no guard, so the user is shown '→ Night  ·  +$-61.15/hr' and the Apply button writes it.
findings.failure: Base rate $65.15 read from 'Pay Rate: $65.15 Hourly'; a row 'PD Night 4.00 36.00 144.00' classifies as 'night' and yields da = 4.00 - 65.15 = -61.15. Review sheet shows '+$-61.15/hr'; after Apply, every night shift prices at (65.15 - 61.15) = $4.00/hr, so a 12h night reads '+$48 gross' in the Add-Shift preview and the hero collapses accordingly.
findings.fix: In applyPaystub (and the matching line in PaystubReview), treat a row whose rate is below the base rate as a premium-only line: `const da = s.rate < p.baseRate ? s.rate : s.rate - p.baseRate` (optionally confirmed by `Math.abs(s.rate*s.hours - s.earnings) < 1`), and never write a negative amount. Add a harness case with a premium-only row asserting the night amount lands at +4.00.

findings.title: Hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip shows the uncapped total and disagrees with the Breakdown it links to
findings.where: index.html:3487 (hero chips) vs index.html:1248-1252 (computeNet dispPre/dispPost) and index.html:3980-3990 (Breakdown rows)
findings.detail: computeNet deliberately caps the displayed pre/post-tax rows (`dispPre`, `dispPost`) so Breakdown sums to gross, and clamps `net` at 0 — but it also returns the raw `ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw`, and the hero chip renders `–{fmt(calc.ded)}` unconditionally. The chip is not guarded by `calc.hours>0` the way the Keep chip is. So whenever flat deductions exceed what gross can absorb, the three hero figures stop summing (Gross − chip ≠ take-home) and the chip contradicts the Breakdown rows one tap away.
findings.failure: Nurse sets Pre-tax $300 / Post-tax $50 in Settings and steps to next fortnight (no shifts yet): hero reads 'Projected take-home $0 · Gross $0 · Taxes & deductions –$350'. Tapping 'See the full breakdown' shows Gross $0, 'Add shifts to see your deductions.', Take-home $0 — the $350 has vanished. With one 4h base shift ($261 gross) the chip says –$370 while the Breakdown rows sum to exactly $261.
findings.fix: Render the chip from what was actually taken out of this period's gross: `–{fmt(calc.gross - calc.net)}` (or hide it with the same `calc.hours>0` guard as the Keep chip). Chip-side change only; computeNet's `ded` can stay as the internal figure.

findings.title: 'Pick up a weekend night?' card prices a differential the nurse has switched off or deleted
findings.where: index.html:3434 (sampleWeekendNet) and index.html:3512-3516 (whatif card guard)
findings.detail: `sampleWeekendNet = round(shiftGross(baseRate, differentials['weekend-eve'], {...}) * keepRatio)` reads the weekend-eve entry regardless of its `active` flag, and the card's only guard is `shiftCount>0 && baseRate>0`. Settings lets the nurse toggle weekend-eve off (`tog(k)`) or delete it entirely (`del(k)`, index.html:4716). The Add-Shift sheet the card's 'Try it' button opens filters to `d.active` types (index.html:4098), so the sheet cannot reproduce the number the card promised.
findings.failure: Base $65.15, keepRatio 0.7785, weekend-eve toggled off because her hospital pays no weekend-night premium: card still says 'That's about +$939 take-home'. She taps Try it; the sheet's best available option (Night, +$10) previews '+$702 take-home'. If she deleted weekend-eve instead, the card prices a 'weekend night' at base rate (+$609) while still calling it a weekend night.
findings.fix: Gate the card on `differentials['weekend-eve']?.active` (hide it otherwise, or fall back to the highest active night-type differential), and use that same resolved type when opening the sheet.

findings.title: Hero hours chip renders the raw float sum, so tenth-hour shifts show '36.900000000000006 hrs'
findings.where: index.html:3489 (`{calc.hours} hrs · {periodShiftCount} shifts`) vs index.html:3496 and index.html:3970 which use toFixed
findings.detail: calc.hours is a plain accumulator over `s.hours` (index.html:2795-2802). The hours NumInput (index.html:4226) commits any parseFloat value — `step="0.5"` is only a spinner hint — and Kronos-style timekeeping rounds to tenths, so 12.3h / 8.1h entries are realistic. The stats tile and Year view both format hours with `toFixed(h%1?1:0)`; the hero chip is the one surface that prints the float directly. Verified in Node: 12.3+12.3+12.3 = 36.900000000000006; 8.1+8.2 = 16.299999999999997.
findings.failure: Three 12.3h shifts in the period: hero chip reads '36.900000000000006 hrs · 3 shifts' while the stats tile directly beneath reads '36.9'.
findings.fix: Use the same formatter as the stats tile: `{calc.hours.toFixed(calc.hours%1?1:0)} hrs`.

findings.title: Year view shows an unlabeled gross figure per month directly beside Month-view cells that show take-home
findings.where: index.html:3970 (YearList row) fed by index.html:2769-2779 (yearMonths rollup)
findings.detail: yearMonths sums `shiftGross` + PTO into `g` and YearList renders `{fmt(mm.g)}` with no qualifier. The Month view it sits one tab away from shows every day as `'~'+fmt(round(t.g*keepRatio))` (index.html:3930) and carries a 'Day amounts are estimated take-home' hint; the Year view carries no equivalent 'gross' label. Same month, two dollar figures, only one of them explained.

findings.fix: Either label it (`{fmt(mm.g)} gross`) or render the same estimated take-home the cells use (`'~'+fmt(round(mm.g*keepRatio))`) so the two views agree.

findings.title: keepRatio omits percent-type custom withholdings that computeNet applies, so the preview overstates a shift's take-home for any blob carrying one
findings.where: index.html:2818-2820 (ficaForPreview / keepRatio) vs index.html:1243 (computeNet cw loop); also index.html:3416-3423 (onboarding sampleNet)
findings.detail: computeNet charges `incomeTaxBase * amount/100` for each `{type:'percent'}` entry in customWithholdings, so the marginal keep rate is 1 − (fed+state+fica+Σpct)/100. keepRatio stops at 1 − (fed+state+fica)/100. Every preview surface — Add-Shift 'about +$N take-home', the ≈$/hr line, the goal '(≈N shifts)' text, calendar '~$' cells, Settings' 'typical 12h shifts' count — uses keepRatio, while the hero uses computeNet. Reachability caveat: no current Settings UI creates customWithholdings (setCW is only called from applyData/reset), but sanitizeData preserves the array from any cloud/localStorage blob and computeNet honours it, so a blob written by an earlier build keeps the disagreement live. sampleNet has the same omission.
findings.failure: Blob with customWithholdings:[{name:'Extra fed',amount:5,type:'percent'}], base $50 + $5 night, fed 12 / state 5 / FICA 7.65. Add-Shift preview for a 12h night: 660 × 0.7535 = '+$497 take-home'. Adding it moves the hero by 660 × 0.7035 = $464 — the preview is $33 (7%) high, and the goal line's '≈N shifts' is correspondingly low.
findings.fix: Fold percent entries into keepRatio: `const cwPct = customWithholdings.reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+cwPct)/100);` and add customWithholdings to sampleNet or route it through computeNet. Add a smoke probe seeding a percent withholding and asserting preview vs hero delta.

findings.title: "Take-home per paycheck" for cycles that don't divide 14 is an average that no actual paycheck ever equals, and nothing on screen says so
findings.where: index.html:1281-1298 (patternMetrics span/periods averaging); labels at index.html:4540 (.pl-money "Take-home per paycheck") and index.html:4428 (side-by-side row "Take-home / paycheck")
findings.detail: patternMetrics prices the rotation over lcm(n,14) days and divides by span/14, so for any cycle length that is not 7 or 14 the figure is a mean across several different paychecks. The card and the comparison table both present it as *the* paycheck, with no 'average' or 'ranges from' qualifier, while the calendar hero (calc, index.html:2787-2810) shows each real 14-day period. Ran the real functions: '4 on, 4 off nights' preset, $50 base, default differentials, 12%/5%/FICA standard/$200 pretax: lab shows $3,749 (gross $5,196); after 'Put it on the calendar' the hero shows $4,233, $4,233, $3,265, $3,265 for the next four paychecks. A hand-built 28-day cycle (8 nights in fortnight 1, 4 in fortnight 2 -- a normal self-scheduled month) shows $3,089 in the lab; the hero shows $4,174 then $2,004. For the 28-day case the code comment's rationale ('a cycle that doesn't divide a fortnight') doesn't even apply -- it divides into exactly two paychecks that are simply different.
findings.failure: Nurse picks '4 on, 4 off nights' because the lab says $3,749/paycheck (vs $3,089 for Mon-Wed nights), applies it, and the very first paycheck on the calendar reads $4,233; the third reads $3,265. Neither matches the number she chose on, and the app never told her it was an average. Same in the side-by-side table: an 8-day or 28-day rotation is compared against 7/14-day ones as if the figures were the same kind of number.
findings.fix: Minimal, label-only (no wage-core touch): when lcm(n,14) > 14, caption the .pl-money card and the side-by-side cell, e.g. 'averaged over N paychecks -- checks will vary' (N = lcm(n,14)/14, computable in PatternLab from m.n). Better: have patternMetrics also return periodNetMin/periodNetMax (net of each 14-day window in the span) and show 'between $X and $Y' -- that variant touches patternMetrics and needs the Invariant 3 protocol.

findings.title: Template-brush cells skip the weekend-differential inference the grid hint promises, and are indistinguishable from generic cells that get it
findings.where: index.html:1204 (patternCellShiftType: `if(cell.kind==='fixed') return cell.shiftType;`); hint at index.html:4536; cellLabel/cellColor at index.html:4316-4326
findings.detail: Generic Day/Night brushes resolve to weekend-day / weekend-eve on Sat/Sun (index.html:1205-1211). A cell painted with a template brush ('tpl:<id>', built at index.html:4350-4358 as kind:'fixed') keeps the template's shiftType verbatim, so a 'My nights' template (shiftType 'night') on Saturday is priced at the plain night differential. The hint under the grid reads, for every brush, 'Weekend days pick up your weekend differentials automatically.' Once painted the two cells are identical: cellLabel gives 'Night 12h from 7:00 PM' for both (differentials.night.name === 'Night'), cellColor gives differentials.night.color for both, same glyph. Ran it: Fri/Sat/Sun nights, 7-day cycle, $50 base, defaults -- generic brush: gross $4,632, net $3,324, calendar types weekend-eve/night/weekend-eve; template brush: gross $4,320, net $3,089, calendar types night/night/night. $312 per paycheck, ~$8.1k/yr, from a brush choice the UI says makes no difference. The exact-type semantics match calendar quick-fill (index.html:2922), so the arithmetic is deliberate; the hint and the indistinguishable cells are the defect.
findings.failure: Nurse saves her usual 'Night 12h' template, paints Fri-Sun with it because it's the brush with her name on it, reads the hint that weekends pick up her weekend differentials, and the lab under-quotes her rotation by ~$312 per paycheck; after apply, every Sat/Sun shift on the calendar is typed 'night' rather than 'weekend-eve' and the hero agrees with the low number.
findings.fix: Either (a) make the hint brush-aware and mark fixed cells (e.g. the ⚡ glyph or the template name in cellLabel) so a template-painted weekend visibly keeps its exact type, or (b) in patternCellShiftType let a fixed cell whose shiftType is 'base' or 'night' go through the same weekend inference as the generic kinds (an explicitly weekend-typed template still keeps its type). (b) changes displayed dollars via patternCellShiftType/planPatternApply, not the listed wage-core functions, but should still get a harness assertion (generic vs template brush on a Saturday).

findings.title: Goal line prints "about 1 years" when a goal takes 26-27 paychecks
findings.where: index.html:4339 (fmtMonths inside PatternLab)
findings.detail: `mo<12 ? ... : \`about ${Math.round(mo/12*10)/10} years\`` -- for n=26 paychecks mo is exactly 12, so the branch yields 'about 1 years'; n=27 also rounds to 1. Ran fmtMonths over 1..52: 25 -> 'about 12 months', 26 -> 'about 1 years', 27 -> 'about 1 years', 52 -> 'about 2 years'. Twenty-six paychecks is exactly one year on this app's own 26-per-year model (yearNet = periodNet*26), so a goal sized to a year's take-home hits this case precisely.

findings.title: Sheet defaults to shiftType 'night' even when Night is toggled off, and prices the hidden differential
findings.where: index.html:4077 (useState('night')), :4099 (active chip filter), :4104-4105 (preview), :1119-1124 (hourlyRate ignores `active`)
findings.detail: AddShiftSheet initialises `shiftType` to the literal 'night' (line 4077) and never reconciles it with the chip list, which is filtered to `d.active` (line 4099). There is no useEffect in the component (checked 4075-4300). `hourlyRate` (1119-1124) does not consult `active`, so `differentials['night']` with `active:false` still adds its amount. The pattern lab does honour the flag — `patternCellShiftType` (1206-1212) prices a night cell as 'base' when Night is inactive — so the two surfaces disagree on the same setup. Settings (4712) and onboarding (5779) both expose the Night switch, so this is one tap away from the default.
findings.failure: Base $50, Night switched off in Settings or onboarding. Tap '+ Log a shift': no shift-type chip is highlighted, yet the preview reads '+$720 gross · about +$561 take-home' (60×12 × 0.7785). Tapping 'Add shift' without touching a chip saves a 'night' shift; the ON THIS DAY row reads 'Night ×12h', the hero rises by $720 and the calendar cell shows ~$561. A day shift at her rate is $600 gross / ~$467 take-home, so every quick log is $120 high on a differential she turned off.
findings.fix: Initialise from the first active, non-overtime key: `useState(()=>{ const a=Object.entries(differentials).find(([k,d])=>d.active&&k!=='overtime'); return a?a[0]:'base'; })` — or, equivalently, derive `active` first and seed from `active[0]`. Add a harness assertion: toggle Night off, open the sheet, assert a chip is `aria-pressed` and the preview equals base×12×keepRatio. (Whether an inactive differential should keep paying on already-logged shifts in calc/statOf is a separate product call; this fix does not touch that.)

findings.title: ≈$/hr take-home is computed from the dollar-rounded net, so identical rates show different cents for different lengths
findings.where: index.html:4105 (previewNet = Math.round(...)) and :4246 (fmt2(previewNet/hours))
findings.detail: `previewNet` is rounded to whole dollars at 4105 for the '+$' headline, then reused as the numerator at 4246 and formatted with `fmt2` to two decimals. The rounding error (up to $0.50) is divided by `hours`, giving up to ±$0.04/hr at 12h, ±$0.06 at 8h and ±$0.125 at 4h — presented as exact cents on a line whose stated purpose is 'compare pickups at a glance'.
findings.failure: Base $47.30, Night +$10, default taxes (keepRatio 0.7785). 12h: 687.60 gross → 535.30 → rounds to 535 → '$44.58/hr'. 8h: 458.40 → 356.86 → rounds to 357 → '$44.63/hr'. Same hourly rate, two different figures; the true value is $44.61 for both. A nurse choosing between an 8 and a 12 sees a 5-cent/hr edge that does not exist.
findings.fix: Keep the rounded value for the headline but divide the unrounded product: `const previewNetExact = previewGross*keepRatio; … fmt2(previewNetExact/hours)`. Same for the goal percentages at 4248 if desired. Sheet-only, no wage-core function touched.

findings.title: Goal with target 0 renders 'Infinity% (≈0 shifts)' in the sheet preview, then vanishes on reload

findings.detail: `addGoal` (4683-4684) requires `t>0`, but `updGoalTarget` (4686) accepts whatever NumInput commits, and NumInput (4016-4027) commits `min` (=0, per the goal row at 4757) on an emptied field. findings.failure: Settings → Savings goals → clear the amount field of 'Car' (blur commits 0). Open any day: the preview reads 'toward your goal: Car Infinity% (≈0 shifts)'. Reopen the app later: the 'Car' goal is gone with no message.

findings.title: keepRatio omits percent-type custom withholdings that computeNet applies, so the sheet preview, calendar day amounts and goal shift-counts overstate take-home relative to the hero/breakdown
findings.where: index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio) vs :1243 (computeNet cw loop); consumers at :4105, :3919/:3933, :4747
findings.detail: `keepRatio = 1 - (federal+state+fica)/100` is the marginal rate used by the Add-shift preview (4105), the calendar `~$` day amounts (3919, 3933), the onboarding sample (3434) and Settings' '≈N typical 12h shifts' (4747). `computeNet` (1231-1250) additionally subtracts `customWithholdings` — percent entries scale with income-tax base exactly like fed/state, so they belong in the marginal rate. There is no in-app editor for custom withholdings (grep: `setCW` is passed to Settings at 4676 but never used; the only writers are `applyData` 2318 via Import JSON and the sanitizer 1031-1038), so the only entry path today is Import JSON or a blob written by an older build. The Breakdown does surface the row as 'Other withholdings' (3987), so a user who has one sees the two surfaces disagree.
findings.failure: Import JSON with `customWithholdings:[{name:'City tax',amount:2,type:'percent'}]`. Breakdown lists 'Other withholdings'. Base $50, Night +$10, 12h: sheet says 'about +$561 take-home'; the hero actually rises by $546 (keep 0.7585). Every day cell and the '≈N shifts to reach this' goal count are ~2.6% high; the sheet's own goal percentages disagree with the hero's period total.
findings.fix: Fold percent withholdings into the preview rate: `const cwPct = (customWithholdings||[]).reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+cwPct)/100);` with `customWithholdings` in scope at 2820. keepRatio is not one of the named wage-core functions, but it changes displayed take-home on three surfaces, so run the hero/breakdown equality assertion against the deployed build with a seed that has no custom withholdings (must be byte-identical) and one that does (expected to differ by the withheld percent).

findings.title: poster_key is reversible: member user_ids and the board creator's id are readable, and the salt is a public constant
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:59-69 ("see co-members" policy + full-table grants on swap_members and swap_groups), :158 (poster_key derivation); live-verified column grants on project mnnlgcxnvodjwlhhiphq
findings.detail: Live, `authenticated` holds SELECT on swap_members(group_id, joined_at, user_id) and swap_groups(id, name, invite_code, created_by, created_at), and the "see co-members" policy returns every member row of every group the caller is in. swap_board() derives `poster_key = substr(md5(author::text || group_id::text || 'scrubpay-swaps'), 1, 8)`. The salt is a string constant in a public repo (github.com/patrick222-dotcom/705-v1 answers `"private": false`), group_id is known to every member, and md5 is a browser one-liner. So `supabase.from('swap_members').select('user_id,joined_at').eq('group_id',G)` yields the N candidate authors; hashing each gives a complete poster_key -> user_id table for the board. Binding a uuid to a person: swap_groups.created_by names the board creator outright (the one who sent everyone the link); joined_at orders the others against who-got-the-link-when; and a single confirmed match pins uid <-> display_name permanently (reveal returns post_id -> name and that post's key was on the board). The migration comment at :155-157 says "Not reversible" and the 2026-07-30 audit checked only that the `author` column can't be selected -- nobody tested rebuilding the key from readable columns. The client never selects from swap_members (only the insert at index.html:1706) and reads only id,name,invite_code (+ order by created_at) from swap_groups (index.html:1675, 1719), so both grants are pure over-exposure.
findings.failure: A nurse posts "give up Fri 9/19 night" after the app tells her "Posted -- your unit sees it anonymously." (index.html:5062). Any co-member with devtools runs one REST select and one md5 loop and knows which uuid posted it; if she created the board, `created_by` names her with no inference at all. Every post she makes in that group is tagged to her from then on -- the feature's core promise is false.
findings.fix: Step 1, grants only (no key change, no client change): `revoke select, update on public.swap_members from authenticated;` (keep insert -- the client's insert at index.html:1706 sends Prefer: return=minimal, and is_swap_member/join_swap_group run as definer) and `revoke select, update on public.swap_groups from authenticated; grant select (id, name, invite_code, created_at) on public.swap_groups to authenticated;`. Step 2: stop deriving the key from a public constant -- keep a per-group random secret in a table with no grants to anon/authenticated and read it inside swap_board (definer), so a leaked uid can never be turned into a key. Nothing persists poster_key client-side (it is recomputed from each board fetch), so changing the derivation has no data impact. Add two probes to the RLS audit: as member A, `select user_id from swap_members` must be 403; `select created_by from swap_groups` must be 403.

findings.title: propose_swap never checks the caller is a leg: any member can reserve and hide any two posts on the board
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:245-265 (propose_swap); live pg_get_functiondef is identical
findings.detail: The RPC validates membership, 2-3 legs, and that each post is open and in the group -- but never that auth.uid() authors any of the legs. The only thing keeping proposals to "matches involving me" is the client: computeSwapSuggestions (index.html:1763-1835) only emits suggestions with a 'me' leg and doPropose (index.html:5079-5099) passes them through. Any member can call `supabase.rpc('propose_swap',{g, post_ids:[x,y]})` with any two open post ids returned by swap_board. Each call flips both posts to 'proposed': swap_board (:164) then hides them from everyone but their authors, openPosts (index.html:5302) drops them, and computeSwapSuggestions ignores them; the two authors get a "WAITING ON 2 OF 2 TO ACCEPT" card pairing them with a stranger's unrelated post. The proposer is not a party, so they can neither see nor decline it -- only the victims can (decline_swap_match) -- and the attacker re-proposes on the next 15s poll. No rate limit, no per-user cap on open matches, and status 'expired' exists but nothing ever sets it.
findings.failure: One member with the invite code pairs every open post on the board in a loop from the console: the board reads "Nothing posted yet" for the whole unit and every poster is stuck declining nonsense matches that come straight back. Selectively: lock every other 'give' for Friday so only their own remains visible to the colleague who wants it.
findings.fix: In propose_swap, after the foreach loop and before `return m`: `if not exists (select 1 from swap_match_legs where match_id = m and leg_user = auth.uid()) then raise exception 'not_a_party'; end if;` -- the exception rolls back the match, legs and status flips. Optionally cap concurrent 'proposed' matches per proposer (e.g. 5) in the same function. Add an audit probe: as member C, propose posts by A and B only -> must raise not_a_party and leave both posts 'open'.

findings.title: Direct UPDATE on swap_matches.status bypasses decline_swap_match and leaves the other party's post stuck 'proposed' forever
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:201-205 ("parties decline matches" UPDATE policy) and :233-235 (grant update (status) on swap_matches); live-verified
findings.detail: decline_swap_match (:273-282) is the documented exclusive decline path (comment at :126-127) because it releases the legs' posts back to 'open' in the same transaction. But the grant + policy also let any party `PATCH /rest/v1/swap_matches?id=eq.M {status:'declined'}` directly. After that the posts stay 'proposed' permanently: decline_swap_match(M) now raises match_not_proposed at :278 before reaching the release at :279; "update own posts" USING requires status='open' (:130) so the author can neither withdraw nor edit; propose_swap refuses it (post_unavailable); openPosts never renders it. The client never uses the direct path (index.html:1938-1944 calls the RPC), so this grant is exercised only by a hand-crafted request or a future client that does it the obvious way.
findings.failure: A party declines by direct PATCH. The other nurse sees "DECLINED", then her give-up post has vanished from the board with no Withdraw button, no way to re-propose it and no error -- the only recovery is to post the same shift again, leaving a permanent orphan row.
findings.fix: `revoke update on public.swap_matches from authenticated; drop policy "parties decline matches" on public.swap_matches;` -- the security-definer RPC needs neither. Audit probe: as a party, direct PATCH status='declined' must be denied (0 rows / 403), then decline_swap_match must still release the posts.

findings.title: "Apply to my calendar" writes another member's unvalidated shift_meta into the victim's shifts
findings.where: index.html:5280-5290 (doApplyPlan), specifically :5285
findings.detail: shift_meta is free-form jsonb authored by another member: the insert grant (001:142-143) and policy (:120-122) accept any JSON under 500 bytes, including scalars, and match_details passes it through verbatim. doApplyPlan pushes `{shiftType:meta.shiftType, hours:meta.hours, start:meta.start}` straight into saveDayShifts -> setShifts (index.html:2857-2858) with no coercion; sanitizeData (:953-986) runs only on load. Until the next load the hero and breakdown compute `shiftGross(baseRate, differentials[s.shiftType], s)` (:1290, :2646, :2775, :2795) with whatever `hours` was sent: a string -> NaN, 1e6 -> millions, a scalar shift_meta -> undefined -> NaN; `h+=s.hours` (:2646) concatenates. The debounced save persists the row; on the next open sanitizeData (:976-977) drops it. Display-only helpers are safe -- giveMetaLine (:4067-4071) and fmtTime12 (:4039-4040, TIME_RE :738) coerce, so the board render itself cannot be crashed this way.
findings.failure: After a confirmed pickup the nurse taps "Add to my calendar": the hero take-home reads "$NaN" (or an absurd figure) for the rest of the session, the malformed shift is synced to the cloud, and when she reopens the app the shift she just picked up is silently gone from her calendar.
findings.fix: In doApplyPlan (before the push at :5285) accept incoming.shift_meta only if it is an object with `typeof shiftType==='string'`, `Number(hours)` finite and in (0,24], and `start` absent or matching TIME_RE; otherwise toast the existing "copy the plan instead" message and return. Server side, add a CHECK on swap_posts.shift_meta guarded by jsonb_typeof so the cast never throws: `shift_meta is null or (jsonb_typeof(shift_meta)='object' and jsonb_typeof(shift_meta->'shiftType')='string' and jsonb_typeof(shift_meta->'hours')='number' and (shift_meta->>'hours')::numeric between 0.1 and 24)`. Neither change touches shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet or the sanitizeData coercions.

findings.title: anon keeps EXECUTE on all eight RPCs and full column grants on all six swap tables; join_swap_group is an unauthenticated invite-code oracle
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:82-83, 166-167, 266-267, 283-284, 300-301, 338-339 (revoke ... from public) and :68-69 (grants with no preceding revoke); live-verified via has_function_privilege and information_schema.column_privileges
findings.detail: Supabase's default privileges grant anon and authenticated ALL on new tables and EXECUTE on new functions at creation time; `revoke ... from public` does not touch those explicit role grants. Live: anon can EXECUTE all eight RPCs and holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on every column of all six tables -- including swap_posts.author, swap_match_legs.leg_user, swap_matches.proposed_by and swap_members.user_id; authenticated additionally holds UPDATE on swap_groups and swap_members that the migration never granted. RLS is enabled on all six and every policy is `to authenticated`, so anon is denied at the row level today and the stray UPDATEs have no policy. The one live consequence: join_swap_group as anon runs the definer lookup and then `insert into swap_members(..., auth.uid())` hits the NOT NULL constraint -- a real code returns 23502, a wrong one returns P0001 'invalid_code'. That is an unauthenticated, unrate-limited oracle over the code space (32^6 ~= 1.07e9 with the client alphabet at index.html:1592) -- impractical to sweep today, but the code is the board's only secret and the check costs nothing. docs/swap-board.md's "author ... is 403 for everyone" holds only for authenticated; one future `to public`/`to anon` policy (a public-preview feature, say) would hand the whole author column to the anon key. The doc's statement that the 16 advisor WARNs "are the design" contradicts the migration's own revoke.
findings.failure: A script holding only the public anon key can confirm which 6-character codes are live boards without ever signing up, then sign up any email and join; and the anonymity columns are one mistaken policy away from being readable with the anon key.
findings.fix: New migration 004: `revoke all on public.swap_posts, public.swap_matches, public.swap_match_legs, public.swap_members, public.swap_groups, public.swap_profiles from anon;` `revoke execute on function public.join_swap_group(text), public.swap_board(uuid), public.propose_swap(uuid,uuid[]), public.decline_swap_match(uuid), public.match_details(uuid), public.reveal_match(uuid), public.is_swap_member(uuid), public.is_match_party(uuid) from anon;` `revoke update on public.swap_groups, public.swap_members from authenticated;` and in join_swap_group open with `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception 'invalid_code'; end if;` so both outcomes read identically. Re-run the advisor: the 8 anon WARNs should disappear. Update docs/swap-board.md accordingly.

findings.title: MAX_BLOB_BYTES is enforced only in the browser; user_data.data has no server-side size bound, so one signed-in account can fill the shared free-tier database
findings.where: supabase/migrations/000_core.sql:27 (data jsonb, no CHECK); confirmed live via pg_constraint — user_data carries only PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY and UNIQUE(user_id), no trigger. Client side: index.html:2464 (the only size check), index.html:2496 (pagehide flush) and index.html:2512 (retrySync) call saveToSupabase without it; saveToSupabase itself at index.html:1324-1344 does no size check.
findings.detail: The 512KB cap that CLAUDE.md calls the 'free-tier guard' is a JavaScript comparison in the debounced save effect. The table has no `pg_column_size(data)` CHECK (compare `events.props`, which does have one in the same migration), and RLS only constrains *which row* an authenticated user may write, not *how big*. Since the Google OAuth app is In production, any Google account is a valid `authenticated` caller against the public anon key. Even inside the app the cap is not actually held: when the debounce path trips it, it toasts 'cloud sync paused' and returns, but the `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` flush (2496) and the manual retry (2512) both call saveToSupabase directly with the same oversized `snapshotRef`/`serializeState()` and write it anyway. Separately, the check compares `JSON.stringify(...).length` (UTF-16 code units) against a byte budget, so non-ASCII notes can be ~3x the intended bytes before it trips.
findings.failure: A hostile (or merely curious) signed-in user issues `POST /rest/v1/user_data` (Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, on_conflict=user_id) with the public anon key + their own JWT and `data` = tens of MB of random base64 (incompressible, so TOAST does not shrink it), repeating the update to leave dead tuples behind. Nothing in Postgres refuses it. The free-tier project crosses its 500MB database quota and Supabase drops it to read-only: every other user's `saveToSupabase` then fails on every edit, each device falls into the failed-save backup mode with the sync-error badge, and cross-device sync stops for everyone until the owner intervenes in the dashboard. In-app variant a real user would see: after the 'cloud sync paused' toast, backgrounding the tab silently uploads the oversized blob the toast just said was not being uploaded.
findings.fix: Add migration 004 (000 is never back-edited): `alter table public.user_data add constraint user_data_data_size check (pg_column_size(data) <= 524288), add constraint user_data_data_is_object check (jsonb_typeof(data) = 'object');` — matches the pattern already used for `events.props`. Then move the size check into `saveToSupabase` itself (return null and logClientError when `new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(data)).length > MAX_BLOB_BYTES`) so the flush and retry paths share it, and treat a 23514 from the server like any other failed save (backup + syncError), which the existing branch already does.

findings.title: sanitizeData passes differential `color` through unvalidated; it lands in `style={{background:…}}` under a CSP that allows `img-src https:`, so an imported JSON file can plant a persistent tracking beacon
findings.where: index.html:1039-1046 (differentials branch: `dd[k] = {...v, amount, type}` keeps any `color`); rendered at index.html:3535, 4181, 4195, 4209, 4713, 5776 as `background:` and 3574, 3929 as `color:`; CSP at index.html:6 (`img-src 'self' data: https:`).
findings.detail: The sanitizer's contract (comment at 947-952) is that a blob from cloud, localStorage or imported JSON is coerced into safe shapes before reaching React state. `amount` and `type` are coerced, but `color` is spread through as-is, and `applyData` (2323) merges it over DIFF_DEFAULTS. React assigns inline styles through the CSSOM, so a value like `url(https://attacker.example/p.gif)` is a valid `background` and the browser fetches it; the `<meta>` CSP explicitly allows any https image host. Because the differential is saved into the user_data blob, the fetch recurs on every device, on every app open, for every calendar cell that shows a shift of that type. No script executes and no wage data is in the request — what leaks is IP, user-agent, timing and a per-open ping to a third party the nurse never chose. The only realistic delivery is 'Import data' with a .json someone else prepared (importData at ~3005 hands the parsed file straight to applyData).
findings.failure: A nurse imports a colleague's exported JSON (or a file that claims to be one). One differential in it has `color: 'url(https://x.example/t)'`. From then on every render of her calendar, template chips and Settings rows makes a request to x.example, on every phone and laptop she signs into, until she notices the dot for that shift type looks wrong and re-picks its colour.
findings.fix: In the differentials branch of sanitizeData, after the existing `dd[k] = {...}` assignment (leave that statement untouched so the amount/type coercions are not edited), add `if(!(typeof dd[k].color==='string' && /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.test(dd[k].color))) delete dd[k].color;` so applyData's merge falls back to the DIFF_DEFAULTS colour. Add a smoke assertion that a blob with `color:'url(https://x)'` renders the default `#8A93A6`, and negative-test it.

findings.title: A shift whose shiftType is an Object.prototype property name (`constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`…) survives sanitizeData and poisons every gross/take-home sum for its pay period to $0
findings.where: index.html:967-978 (shift filter accepts any string shiftType); lookups without an own-property guard at index.html:1290 (patternMetrics), 2646, 2775, 2795 (calc/statOf), 3419, 4104 (preview); hourlyRate at index.html:1124-1129.
findings.detail: `differentials` is a plain object built by `{...DIFF_DEFAULTS, ...}` (applyData 2323-2326), so `differentials['constructor']` is `Object` and `differentials['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype` — both truthy. `hourlyRate(base, Object)` falls to `base + diff.amount` = `base + undefined` = NaN; `shiftGross` returns NaN; `calc`'s `gross += NaN` poisons the whole period, and `fmt`/`fmt2` (`Number(n||0)`) then render NaN as `$0`. The sanitizer's stated purpose (947-950) is precisely that a corrupt or hostile blob 'must never … silently corrupt every calculation with string/NaN fields', and legitimate unknown shiftTypes (e.g. a deleted custom differential) already fall back to base rate because `differentials[k]` is undefined — only inherited property names break that fallback. Reachable via the JSON import path or a direct API write to the user's own row; both persist, so the damage survives reloads and syncs to every device.
findings.failure: A nurse imports a JSON file containing one shift `{shiftType:'constructor', hours:12}` in the current fortnight. The hero, the Gross/Taxes/Keep chips, the breakdown and the pattern-lab readout for that pay period all show $0 instead of her real figures, on every device, with nothing on the calendar cell that looks abnormal (the dot just takes the fallback grey).
findings.fix: Route every `differentials[s.shiftType]` lookup through one helper, e.g. `const diffFor = (diffs,k) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(diffs,k) ? diffs[k] : undefined;`, and use it at 1290, 2646, 2775, 2795, 3419, 4104 (and the display-only lookups at 3028, 3535, 3929, 4069, 4181, 4195-4196, 4324 for consistency). Do not reject unknown shiftTypes in sanitizeData — that would drop real shifts whose custom differential was deleted. Because this touches calc/statOf/patternMetrics, run the wage-math probes and the hero/breakdown equality assertion against the deployed build, plus a new probe asserting a `constructor` shift is paid at base rate.

findings.title: ical-proxy accepts the public anon key: verify_jwt does not mean "signed-in user"
findings.where: supabase/functions/ical-proxy/index.ts:8-9 and :46-59 (no role/user check anywhere in the handler); anon key shipped at index.html:616
findings.detail: The function's header comment and CLAUDE.md both claim `verify_jwt` restricts the proxy to signed-in users ("an unauthenticated POST is 401, so it is not an open proxy"). That is only true for a request with NO Authorization header. The Supabase gateway's verify_jwt checks the signature, and the project's anon key is itself a JWT signed with the same secret (`role: anon`, exp 2036). Live probe against the deployed function (version 1, byte-identical to the repo copy): no header -> 401 UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key from index.html>` with `{"url":"https://www.google.com/"}` -> 422 not_a_calendar, i.e. the handler ran and fetched the upstream. The handler never inspects the JWT's `role`/`sub` (index.ts:46-59 go straight from body parsing to the allowlist), so anyone who has viewed the page source can drive it. The allowlist still holds (169.254.169.254 -> 403), so this is not an internal SSRF, but the second allowlist entry `/^www\.google\.com$/` (index.ts:22) has no path constraint, so the project is an anonymous relay for arbitrary google.com URLs and any public/secret Google Calendar feed, with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (index.ts:31) so it works from any web page.
findings.failure: A script with the anon key (harvested by any of the crawlers already hitting badgebudget.com) loops POSTs at a large public Google calendar feed: each call is a free-tier invocation plus up to 2MB of egress. The project hits the free-tier egress/compute cap, and every real nurse loses cloud sync and calendar sync until the next billing window, or the owner pays. The intended control ("only a signed-in user can call this") is simply not in force.
findings.fix: In the handler, before the allowlist: read `req.headers.get('Authorization')`, decode the bearer JWT payload (the gateway has already verified its signature) and return 401 unless `payload.role === 'authenticated'` and `payload.sub` is a UUID; or equivalently build a supabase client with that header and require `auth.getUser()` to return a user. Then correct the two comments (index.ts:8-9, CLAUDE.md Supabase section) and add the negative test to the ship ritual: `curl` with the anon key must return 401. While there, pin both Google entries to the `/calendar/ical/` path prefix so `www.google.com` is not a general-purpose relay.

findings.title: Previous account's secret feed URL survives a stalled sign-out and is shown/saved for the next account on the same device
findings.where: index.html:2529-2540 handleSignOut (does not clear icalSub/icalUrl/hydratedUserId/icalSyncedForUser); index.html:2335-2340 resetToDefaults (same omission); index.html:2441 hydration effect `catch(_){ return; }`
findings.detail: The only place `icalSub`/`icalUrl` are cleared on sign-out is the SIGNED_OUT branch of onAuthStateChange (index.html:2417). `handleSignOut` exists precisely because that event "won't fire if signOut stalled" (its own comment) and it mirrors the branch for every field except the four iCal ones; `resetToDefaults` (which it calls) also skips them. So after a stalled sign-out (the WebKit lock deadlock this codebase already documents) user A's bearer credential stays in React state. When user B signs in on the same tab, hydrateFromCloud sets hydratedUserId, the effect at index.html:2431-2450 calls loadIcalSub(B); if that throws (network blip) it `return`s before the `setIcalSub(sub); setIcalUrl(...)` line, leaving A's URL and subscription object in place. Settings renders the CALENDAR SYNC block for any truthy `user` (index.html:4785) with `value={icalUrl}` (4790), 'Sync now' calls runIcalSync which resolves `url` from `icalSub.icalUrl` (3254), and 'Update link' calls saveIcalSub(user.id=B, url=A's) (3300). Even on the success path there is a render window between setHydratedUserId(B) and loadIcalSub resolving where B's Settings shows A's URL.
findings.failure: On a shared unit iPad: nurse A signs out (sign-out stalls, 3s timeout), nurse B signs in on flaky Wi-Fi so loadIcalSub fails. B opens Settings and sees A's secret Google Calendar address in the input; tapping 'Sync now' pulls A's shifts into B's questionnaire; tapping 'Update link' stores A's feed under B's account permanently, so B's app re-fetches A's private calendar on every open from then on.
findings.fix: Add `setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl(''); setHydratedUserId(null); icalSyncedForUser.current = null;` to handleSignOut (or into resetToDefaults, which both sign-out paths call). In the hydration effect, make the catch clear state too (`setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl('');`) instead of returning with whatever was there, and key the effect so a stale subscription from a different uid can never be reused: in runIcalSync/onSaveIcalUrl, refuse when `icalSub.userId !== user.id` (store the uid on the icalSub object). Harness: seed state as A, simulate a rejected signOut and a rejected loadIcalSub for B, assert the input is empty.

findings.title: webcal:// (and http://) feed links pass the client check but are rejected by the proxy forever
findings.where: supabase/functions/ical-proxy/index.ts:57-58; index.html:3245-3251 providerOf and :3293-3306 onSaveIcalUrl
findings.detail: Not a security hole, but a defect inside the SSRF guard that the client and server disagree on. The proxy does `target.protocol = "https:"` on a `webcal:` URL; per the WHATWG URL spec the protocol setter refuses to change a non-special scheme to a special one, so it is a no-op (verified in Node: protocol stays `webcal:`) and the next line returns 400 https_only. Live probe with the deployed function and `{"url":"webcal://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/x/basic.ics"}` -> 400 {"error":"https_only"}. The client's providerOf strips `webcal:` only for host detection and onSaveIcalUrl saves and syncs the raw string, so the subscription is persisted in a state that can never succeed. `http://calendar.google.com/...` behaves the same way (providerOf has no scheme check).
findings.failure: A nurse pastes a webcal://calendar.google.com/... link (the form Apple Calendar and many share sheets produce). She sees 'Calendar link saved.' followed immediately by "Couldn't reach your calendar. Check the link and try again.", and every subsequent app-open sync silently fails; the link looks correct to her so there is nothing to fix.
findings.fix: In the proxy, rewrite the string before parsing: `if (/^webcal:/i.test(raw)) raw = 'https:' + raw.slice(7);` then `new URL(raw)`. In onSaveIcalUrl, normalise the same way before saving so the stored ical_url is always https, and have providerOf return null for any scheme other than https/webcal so the toast names the problem at save time. Add the webcal case to the harness sync assertions.

findings.title: Google sign-in runs the OAuth *implicit* flow, not PKCE — tokens land in a URL fragment that stays one Back-press away in browser history
findings.where: index.html:610-615 (createClient with no options) and index.html:4619-4625 (handleGoogleAuth / signInWithOAuth)
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md and the invite-link comment at index.html:1602-1605 ("supabase-js PKCE puts its own `?code=` here") both say the Google path is PKCE. It is not. The vendored supabase-js 2.45.4 (auth-js 2.65.0) sets `DEFAULT_AUTH_OPTIONS={autoRefreshToken:!0,persistSession:!0,detectSessionInUrl:!0,flowType:"implicit"}`, and `createClient(url, key)` at 610-615 passes no `auth` options, so `signInWithOAuth` sends no code_challenge and Supabase redirects back to `redirectTo` with `#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&provider_token=…` in the fragment. auth-js consumes that fragment and clears it with `window.location.hash=""` (verified in the bundle; the PKCE branch instead does `searchParams.delete("code")` + `history.replaceState`). The clear happens only after an awaited `/auth/v1/user` round-trip, i.e. normally after the page's `load` event — and I verified in the sandbox Chromium (iPhone 13 profile) that a post-load `location.hash=''` grows `history.length` 2→3 and `history.back()` restores the full `#access_token=…&refresh_token=…` URL. (When the round-trip beats `load`, Chromium converts it to a replacement and no entry is left — so it is timing-dependent, not guaranteed.) The fragment refresh token stays valid until the first rotation (~1h) or a server-side sign-out.
findings.failure: A nurse signs in with Google on a shared unit workstation or a borrowed phone, then walks away. Whoever next touches the browser presses Back (or opens History) and sees `badgebudget.com/#access_token=…&refresh_token=…` in the address bar; pasting that URL into a tab (or calling /auth/v1/token with the refresh_token) gives them her session and her pay history for up to an hour, and a colleague scrolling the shared machine's history days later still sees the tokens in the list even after they have expired.
findings.fix: Opt into PKCE: `window.supabase.createClient(url, key, {auth:{flowType:'pkce'}})` at index.html:611. auth-js then returns `?code=` and scrubs it with replaceState (no history entry, no token in any URL); `takeSwapInviteFromUrl` (1619-1629) already writes foreign params like `code` back byte-identical, so the invite flow is unaffected. Re-run the smoke suite's sign-in section and confirm a real Google sign-in on badgebudget.com still lands (the redirect allow list is unchanged). Then correct the PKCE claim in CLAUDE.md → Auth and the comment at 1602-1605.

findings.title: client_error batch can exceed the live `events_props_check` (< 2000 bytes) and is silently dropped after the ring buffer was already cleared
findings.where: index.html:1443-1456 (flushClientErrors) with index.html:1385-1398 (track) and the live constraint `events_props_check CHECK (pg_column_size(props) < 2000)`
findings.detail: `flushClientErrors` ships up to `ERR_FLUSH_CAP`=8 entries, each with a 300-char `msg`, 80-char `src`, `t` and `line`. Measured in the live database: 8 entries at 300 chars = 3,116 jsonb bytes; 6×300 = 2,348; 8×200 = 2,316; 8×170 = 2,060 — all rejected by the CHECK; 5×300 = 1,964 and 8×120 = 1,676 pass. So any batch of ≥6 max-length entries, or 8 entries averaging ≳165 chars, fails with 23514. Max-length entries are the normal case for the errors that matter: `ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch` (index.html:2160) logs `error` plus the JSON-stringified `errorInfo` (a componentStack of hundreds of chars, sliced to 500 in the buffer and 300 in the flush), and PostgREST error objects mirrored from `console.error('Load error:', error)` (1469) run 150-300 chars. `track()` swallows the rejection into `console.debug` (1396), which is not mirrored into the ring buffer, and `__takeErrorLog()` (567-572) already removed the batch before the send — so the loss is total and self-concealing. Live data so far: 11 client_error rows, max 526 bytes, max n=3, so nothing has been lost *yet*; the arithmetic is deterministic for the first bad session.
findings.failure: A nurse hits a React render crash loop (ErrorBoundary fires several times) or a run of failed cloud loads during one visit. On her next app open the flush builds an 8-entry, ~3 KB batch, Postgres rejects it, the ring buffer is already empty, and the owner's `select … where name='client_error'` shows nothing for exactly the session that needed diagnosing — worse than before the telemetry existed, because the local buffer was also drained.
findings.fix: Budget the payload in `flushClientErrors` before calling `track`: cut per-entry `msg` to ~160 chars and drop the oldest entries while `JSON.stringify(props).length > ~1700` (jsonb adds ~5-10% over the text form, so 1,700 text bytes stays under 2,000). Optionally also widen the CHECK in a `004` migration (e.g. `< 4000`) so a stale client can't lose a batch either. Add a smoke assertion that seeds 8 long entries into `scrubpayErrors` and asserts the resulting event body is under the cap.

findings.title: events/feedback INSERT policies accept any `user_id` — attribution is client-asserted, not bound to auth.uid()
findings.where: supabase/migrations/000_core.sql:59-62 and :86-88 (live policies verified: `check=((char_length(name) >= 1) AND (char_length(name) <= 64))` on events, message-length only on feedback); callers index.html:1385-1398 (track) and :1356-1366 (submitFeedback)
findings.detail: Both insert policies check only a length; `user_id` is whatever the client sends. The FK to `auth.users(id)` means the value must be a real user's uuid, and the app itself never surfaces other users' ids (the swap RPCs return `display_name`, not uids), so the attacker needs the uuid from elsewhere — but anyone holding the public anon key who has one can write `signed_in`, `client_error` or `feedback` rows attributed to that user. The ops dashboard's `segment` classifies a device as `insider` from "any anon_id ever seen signed in as one of" the owner accounts, so a single forged `signed_in` row with an insider uuid re-labels an arbitrary anon_id. Every real call site already passes either `null` (index.html:3004, flushes) or the id of the JWT the request carries (2410 `track('signed_in', null, nextId)` fires after the client has installed the new session; 3283 and submitFeedback use `user.id`), so tightening the policy breaks nothing.
findings.failure: Someone with the anon key (it is in the page source) and a known user uuid inserts `{name:'signed_in', user_id:<owner uuid>, anon_id:<their device>}`; the next dashboard snapshot counts their device as an insider and drops it from the public activation funnel, or floods `feedback` with rows that appear to come from a real signed-in nurse and carry her uuid in the owner read.
findings.fix: Migration 004: `alter policy "anyone can insert events" on public.events with check (char_length(name) between 1 and 64 and (user_id is null or user_id = (select auth.uid())))` and the same `(user_id is null or user_id = (select auth.uid()))` clause on `anyone can submit feedback`. Mirror both in 000_core.sql's successor rather than back-editing 000. Negative-test with the anon key: an insert carrying a real uuid must now fail with 42501.

findings.title: poster_key is reversible by any group member: swap_members.user_id and swap_groups.created_by are selectable, and the salt is public
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:68-69 (grants), :158 (salt), :136-137 (the claim); live grants confirmed via information_schema.column_privileges
findings.detail: The anonymity model says the API 'physically cannot return author ids to other members' (001:136-137, docs/swap-board.md:13-16). But `grant select, insert on public.swap_groups` and `grant select, insert, delete on public.swap_members` (001:68-69) are table-wide, so every member can `GET /rest/v1/swap_members?group_id=eq.<g>&select=user_id` (policy 'see co-members' is just is_swap_member) and `select created_by from swap_groups`. Live DB confirms SELECT on both columns for `authenticated`. `poster_key = substr(md5(author::text || group_id::text || 'scrubpay-swaps'),1,8)` (001:158) uses a salt that sits in a public repo (github.com/patrick222-dotcom/705-v1 is visibility:public), so the search space is the <=N co-member uuids, not 2^128 -- a member computes eight md5s and has a poster_key -> user_id table for the whole board. The client never reads either column (index.html:1675/1719 select `id,name,invite_code`; swap_members is only inserted at :1706), so nothing depends on the grant.
findings.failure: (1) With zero preconditions, the board creator (created_by, usually the person who shared the code and is therefore known) is unmasked as the author of every post she makes -- contradicting the in-app promise. (2) After any single confirmed match, reveal_match's display_name -> post_id -> poster_key -> uuid chain names that colleague permanently and across EVERY group they share (uuid is global; the documented known gap at docs/swap-board.md:35-37 was per-group only). Two REST calls with the attacker's own JWT from devtools.
findings.fix: Column-scope the grants (a table-wide grant cannot be partially revoked, so revoke then re-grant): `revoke select on public.swap_members from authenticated; grant select (group_id, joined_at) on public.swap_members to authenticated; revoke select on public.swap_groups from authenticated; grant select (id, name, invite_code, created_at) on public.swap_groups to authenticated;`. RLS policies still evaluate `user_id`/`created_by` (policy expressions are not subject to column privileges). Ship as 004 and add an rls_audit assertion that `select user_id from swap_members` and `select created_by from swap_groups` are 42501 for a member. Second half, dedicated session (Invariant 7): the salt is public, so consider deriving poster_key from a server-side secret (e.g. vault/current_setting) so enumeration alone can never reverse it.

findings.title: ical-proxy accepts the public anon key: verify_jwt gates on a valid project JWT, and the anon key is one
findings.where: supabase/functions/ical-proxy/index.ts:8-9 (the claim), :44-60 (no caller check); anon key at index.html:616
findings.detail: index.ts:8-9 states 'verify_jwt is ON -- only a signed-in ScrubPay user can call this' and CLAUDE.md says 'an unauthenticated POST is 401, so it is not an open proxy'. The gateway only checks the JWT signature; the anon key in index.html:616 (role:anon) is signed by the same project secret. Live probe today: POST with no header -> 401 UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER; POST with `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` and `{"url":"http://example.com"}` -> HTTP 400 `{"error":"https_only"}`, i.e. the function body ran. Nothing inside the function inspects the caller (no auth.getUser, no role claim check).
findings.failure: Anyone who reads the deployed HTML can drive unlimited fetches of any calendar.google.com / www.google.com / *.nursegrid.com URL through Supabase's egress with no account, burning the free-tier Edge Function invocation and egress quota until real users' 'Sync now' starts failing with 'Couldn't reach your calendar'. The allowlist still stops SSRF to internal hosts; what is false is the 'signed-in only' premise the file is built on.
findings.fix: Inside Deno.serve, before the URL checks: read `req.headers.get('authorization')`, decode the JWT payload and reject unless `role === 'authenticated'` (or create a supabase client with the header and require `auth.getUser()` to return a user), returning 401 otherwise. Keep verify_jwt on. Update the comment at index.ts:8-9 and the CLAUDE.md sentence so the next reviewer does not inherit the wrong premise.

findings.title: Raw 'parties decline matches' UPDATE policy bypasses decline_swap_match and strands the other party's post as 'proposed' forever
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:202-205 (policy), :233-235 (update (status) grant), :130 and :277-278 (why it is unrecoverable); live policy confirmed via pg_policies
findings.detail: decline_swap_match() exists precisely so declining releases the reserved posts in one transaction (001:269-282). But the policy 'parties decline matches' plus `grant ... update (status) on swap_matches` still let any party `PATCH /rest/v1/swap_matches?id=eq.<m>` with `{status:'declined'}` directly. That path never touches swap_posts. Afterwards: the author's 'update own posts' USING requires status='open' (001:130) so she cannot withdraw or edit it; decline_swap_match raises match_not_proposed because status is already 'declined' (001:277-278); reveal_match raises match_not_proposed (001:315); the board RPC hides it from everyone else (001:164). The client only ever uses the RPC (index.html:1938-1944; the sole `.from('swap_matches')` is a select at :1882), so the raw path is pure attack surface.
findings.failure: Colleague B, party to a match with A, sends one REST PATCH from devtools. A's give-up post vanishes from the unit's board, shows only in A's own list, cannot be withdrawn, edited or re-proposed, and never comes back -- A's shift is effectively un-swappable until the owner fixes the row in SQL.
findings.fix: `drop policy "parties decline matches" on public.swap_matches; revoke update on public.swap_matches from authenticated;` (re-grant only `select (id, group_id, status, created_at)`). All declines then go through the security-definer RPC. Add an rls_audit assertion that a direct PATCH to status='declined' is 42501 for a party.

findings.title: propose_swap does not require the proposer to be a party to the match it creates
findings.where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:245-265 (propose_swap); live body confirmed to contain no leg_user = auth.uid() gate
findings.detail: The RPC checks membership of g (001:249) and that each post is open and in g (001:253-256), then inserts legs for the posts' authors. It never checks that auth.uid() is one of those authors. The client only proposes trades that 'involve ME' (index.html:1754-1760), so the server is the only place this can be enforced and it is not.
findings.failure: Any member can reserve any two or three other members' open posts into a match none of them asked for (posts flip to 'proposed' and leave the board, 001:258), and re-propose immediately after each decline. Victims see 'someone proposed' with no way to tell it was not the other party. In a 12-bed unit one person can keep the whole board reserved indefinitely.
findings.fix: After the FOREACH loop in propose_swap: `if not exists (select 1 from swap_match_legs where match_id = m and leg_user = auth.uid()) then raise exception 'not_a_party'; end if;` (the insert rolls back with the exception). Optionally also reject arrays with duplicate post_ids and matches whose legs all share one author. Add the case to the swap-matching suite when it is ported to tests/.

findings.title: Deploy workflow runs mutable action tags with pages:write + id-token:write
findings.where: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:30, 33, 48, 54 (actions/checkout@v4, configure-pages@v4, upload-pages-artifact@v3, deploy-pages@v4); ci.yml:29, 32, 56, 59
findings.detail: deploy.yml grants `pages: write` and `id-token: write` (lines 13-16) and resolves four actions by floating major tag. A moved or compromised tag runs with the OIDC token that publishes badgebudget.com. CI's actions run with contents:read only, so the exposure is the deploy job. Already listed in CLAUDE.md under 'CI and the harness' as to-do; recorded here because it is the one place in this slice where what reaches nurses' phones depends on a ref nobody in the repo controls.
findings.failure: A poisoned `actions/deploy-pages` or `upload-pages-artifact` release publishes attacker HTML at badgebudget.com on the next merge; every signed-in nurse who opens the app hands it her session and wage blob, and the SRI/CSP in index.html cannot help because the page itself is replaced.
findings.fix: Pin each `uses:` to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment (e.g. `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.2`), and bump checkout/setup-node off the deprecated Node 20 runtime while doing it. Have scripts/check_build.mjs assert every `uses:` in both workflows matches `@[0-9a-f]{40}` so the pin cannot silently regress.

findings.title: Hero's 'See the full breakdown' / 'Share BadgeBudget' links accidentally inherit the full .hero card style, ballooning them and adding dead scroll space to the very first screen
findings.where: index.html:3491-3492 (className="hero more linklike"); CSS: .linklike padding:0 at 79, .hero padding/border-radius/background/box-shadow at 114, .hero .more at 119
findings.detail: The two footer buttons are given className="hero more linklike" — three independent classes, not a scoped ".hero .more" selector. Because the token "hero" is also the class name of the enclosing card, both buttons literally match the top-level `.hero{background:var(--ink);border-radius:22px;padding:22px 24px;...box-shadow:...}` rule (line 114) in addition to `.hero .more` (119) and `.linklike` (79). `.hero` and `.linklike` have equal CSS specificity (one class each), so the tie is broken by source order, and `.hero` (declared later, at line 114) beats `.linklike`'s `padding:0` (line 79) — the buttons keep `.hero`'s 22px/24px padding, border-radius and box-shadow instead of being flush, padding-free text links. Verified live on an iPhone-13 viewport: document.querySelectorAll('.hero') genuinely returns 3 elements (the card plus both buttons); each button's computed style is 'padding: 22px 24px', height balloons to 59px, and a screenshot shows each rendering as its own visible dark rounded pill with an inset highlight seam nested inside the real hero card, rather than a plain link line.
findings.failure: On every load, the hero card — the first thing a nurse sees, and the thing the whole app is built around — is roughly 120px taller than intended, almost entirely padding around two one-line links. One-handed on a phone, that's extra scrolling distance before she reaches the calendar / '+ Log a shift' controls beneath it, and the two links visually read as broken/unstyled boxes rather than the intended small footer actions.
findings.fix: Stop reusing the literal token "hero" as a class on these buttons — give them a distinct class (e.g. "hero-more") so they no longer match the card-level .hero rule, or restructure so the descendant relationship is expressed purely through DOM nesting rather than a repeated class name.

findings.title: Dollar-amount edit fields in Settings (differential rate, savings-goal target) have a 17px-tall tap target, versus 44px used everywhere else in the same sheet
findings.where: index.html:4715 (differential amount NumInput) and 4754 (goal target NumInput); CSS: .drow .amt / .drow .amt input at 312-313, .danger-link at 423
findings.detail: `.drow .amt{padding:5px 10px}` wraps the number, but `.drow .amt input{width:54px;border:none;background:transparent;...}` sets no padding or min-height on the <input> itself, and the wrapper is a plain <span> (not a <label>), so tapping the padded pill around the number does nothing — only the number glyph itself is live. Measured live in the rendered Settings sheet on an iPhone-13 viewport: each goal-target and differential-rate NumInput is 54x17px (34x17 for a multiplier-type differential), and the adjacent 'Del' button on the same row is 35x39px — both well under the 44px minimum the codebase otherwise enforces (33 other spots in index.html explicitly set minHeight:44), and in visible contrast to the compliant ~42px-tall .inp input fields (line 292, padding:13px 14px) used for base rate, tax %, and bonus $ a few rows above in the same form.
findings.failure: Correcting a savings-goal target or a shift differential's dollar rate one-handed mid-shift means landing a tap inside a 17px-tall strip — under half the app's own stated minimum — and the larger padded pill around it looks tappable but isn't, so a mistap lands nowhere and she has to try again to get the cursor into the number field. The 'Del' button on the same row is likewise a few pixels short of 44px in each dimension.
findings.fix: Give .drow .amt input real padding or min-height:44px so the live hit-box matches the visible pill (or turn the .amt span into a <label> so tapping anywhere in the pill focuses the input), and bump .danger-link to a 44px box on these money-editing rows to match the convention used elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: Calendar scroll box has an absolute 420px height floor that exceeds the entire viewport in landscape
findings.where: index.html:184 (.cal-vscroll), contrast with .sheet/.modal at index.html:396,399
findings.detail: `.cal-vscroll{max-height:60vh;min-height:420px;...}` sets a hard 420px minimum height on the Month-view scroll box, in plain (non-dynamic) `vh`. Elsewhere in this same file the sheet/modal containers were deliberately switched to `dvh` (`.sheet{max-height:92dvh}` line 396, `.modal{max-height:90dvh}` line 399) specifically because mobile browser chrome changes available height — the calendar container is the one scroll surface that was never brought in line with that pattern, and unlike them it also carries a bare pixel floor with no viewport-relative cap under it.
findings.failure: Rotate an iPhone 13 (the project's own test profile) to landscape while on Month view. Landscape viewport height for a phone is typically ~350-390px after Safari's toolbar, well under the 420px the calendar box is forced to occupy. The calendar's own scroll container alone now consumes more vertical space than the entire screen, pushing the greet-row/hero, the +Log a shift button and the bottom nav completely off-screen — a one-handed nurse who rotates her phone (even accidentally) has to scroll the whole page up and down just to see anything besides the calendar grid, including controls that were one glance away in portrait.
findings.fix: Cap `.cal-vscroll` against the real viewport instead of a fixed px floor — e.g. drop `min-height:420px` (or express it as `min(420px, 60dvh)`) and switch `60vh` to `60dvh` so the box shrinks with the actual available height in landscape the same way `.sheet`/`.modal` already do.

findings.title: Pay-period boundary chip inside the scrolling grid is a ~19px-tall tap target with no hit-area expansion

Elsewhere in this exact file, small buttons of similar visual size are deliberately padded out to the 44px minimum with a pseudo-element: `.calnav button` is 36x36 but gets `::after{inset:-5px}` (index.html:161-162) for an effective ~46x46 hit area, and `.period button` is 24x24 but gets `::after{inset:-10px}` (index.html:104-105) for an effective 44x44. She is likely to either miss the chip (nothing happens) or overshoot onto the adjacent day cell, which opens the Add-Shift sheet for the wrong date instead of switching pay periods.
