findings.title: Day-cell tap targets drop to ~42px square at the ≤360px breakpoint this file itself treats as supported small-phone width
findings.where: index.html:221 (.cell), sizing driven by .cal-vscroll padding and .grid gap at index.html:206-212
findings.detail: At the ≤360px breakpoint (the same one index.html:441-448 singles out by name — "Very small phones (≤360px, e.g. iPhone SE)" — for a topbar-padding fix), the Month grid's available width is viewport minus 18px .wrap padding ×2, minus .card's 1px border and 18px padding ×2 (cancelled back out by `.cal-vscroll-wrap{margin:0 -18px}`), minus `.cal-vscroll`'s mobile padding of 8px×2 (line 211) — leaving ~306px for 7 columns with a 2px gap (line 212), i.e. (306-12)/7 ≈ 42px per cell. That's under the 44px tap-target guideline; at ≥375px (a real iPhone SE/6/7/8) the same math clears ~44px, so this only bites below that width.
findings.failure: On a ≤360px-wide Android phone (the class of device the file's own ≤360px media query is written for), the day cells — the single most-used tap target in the whole calendar, used to open every shift — are individually ~2px narrower/shorter than the 44px minimum, with no compensating hit-area expansion the way `.calnav`/`.period` buttons get elsewhere in this file. Marginal, but it's the primary tap surface of the screen shrinking below the line other small controls in this codebase were explicitly tuned to meet.

findings.detail: `.pl-grid` is a 7-column CSS grid with a fixed `gap:5px`, sitting inside `.modal{padding:24px}` (line 399, no per-breakpoint reduction anywhere in the file's three @media blocks at lines 206, 440, 447). findings.title: REPEATS EVERY cycle-length buttons render ~41px tall, under the 44px tap target
findings.where: index.html:4503
findings.detail: The 7/8/14/28-day preset buttons override the shared `.hrs .hc` style (`.hrs .hc{padding:11px;...font-size:14px}`, index.html:323) with an inline `{fontSize:13,padding:'11px 4px'}`. Height ≈ 2×11px padding + 2×1.5px border + ~13×1.2 line-height ≈ 40.6px, below the 44px guideline for a primary choice control at the top of every new-pattern flow.
findings.failure: Picking the rotation length is the first tap a nurse makes when starting a new pattern; a ~41px-tall pill is more likely to be mis-tapped one-handed than the rest of the app's already-borderline `.hc` buttons (which sit at ~41.8px by default but aren't further narrowed).
findings.fix: Drop the inline font/padding override (or raise vertical padding back toward the default ~13px+) so the button reaches 44px tall; if horizontal space for 4 pills plus the custom-length input is the concern, let the row wrap onto two lines instead of shrinking button height.

findings.title: est-banner action buttons are under the 44px tap-target minimum, unlike every other interactive control in this slice
findings.where: index.html:143-144 (.est-banner button / .est-banner button.ghost CSS), rendered at index.html:3470-3475
findings.detail: `.est-banner button{padding:9px 13px;...font-size:12.5px}` (line 143) has no explicit line-height or min-height, so its rendered height is roughly 9+9px padding plus a ~12.5px line box — about 33-35px tall. That's the button a nurse taps to react to a rough/sample estimate: 'Sharpen it'/'Enter my rate' and 'Clear the sample'/'Got it', 8px apart in a `.row{display:flex;gap:8px;...}` (line 142). I checked whether this app compensates for small controls the way it does elsewhere: `.back` (line 368) and `.tg` (line 281) both carry a `::after{position:absolute;...}` hit-slop overlay (lines 369 and 282) that pads their effective tap area out to ~44px, and `.acct-menu button` (line 94) and `.pl-brushes .chip-sel` (line 346) both set `min-height:44px` directly — so the codebase clearly already treats 44px as the bar elsewhere. `.est-banner button` has neither technique.
findings.failure: A nurse reading the est-banner after a rough/sample setup, one-handed, taps to fix her estimate. The two buttons are each ~34px tall with only 8px between them and no invisible hit-slop margin, so a fingertip (which is wider than either button) can land on the wrong one — e.g. tapping 'Got it' (which silently sets estimateMode to '' and dismisses the banner for good) when she meant to tap 'Sharpen it' (which opens Settings), or missing both buttons on the first tap and having to re-aim.
findings.fix: Give `.est-banner button` `min-height:44px` (matching `.acct-menu button` / `.pl-brushes .chip-sel`), or add a `::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:-Npx}` hit-slop overlay the way `.back` and `.tg` already do, and widen the 8px gap between the two banner buttons.

findings.title: Share sheet is the one sheet that doesn't lock background scroll
findings.where: index.html:2596-2600 (body-scroll-lock effect) vs index.html:2228-2230/3657 (showShare state) and index.html:5666-5702 (ShareSheet)

findings.title: Avatar (sole mobile Settings/Sign-out entry point) is a 40px tap target with no hit-area bump, unlike its sibling icon button
findings.where: index.html:86 (.avatar) vs index.html:75-76 (.iconbtn / .iconbtn::after) and index.html:1974-1975 (AccountMenu's avatar button)
findings.detail: `.iconbtn` (the topbar feedback 💬 button) is 40x40 visually but gets `.iconbtn::after{position:absolute;inset:-2px}` (line 76), which is hit-testable and bumps its real tap target to 44x44 — the app clearly knows and applies the 44px minimum. `.avatar` (line 86) is also 40x40 but gets no such pseudo-element or padding; `.acct` (87) adds no padding either. I rendered both in a real browser at 390px width and measured: iconbtn effectively 44x44 (via the -2px inset), avatar exactly 40x40 with no expansion. Per the file's own comment (index.html:80-85), since 2026-09-13 this avatar is "the only route to Settings and Sign out on a phone" below 920px — it absorbed the old separate gear/sign-out icon buttons.
findings.failure: A nurse reaching one-handed for the top-right corner to open Settings or sign out gets a target 4px narrower on each axis than Apple's 44pt minimum and than the feedback button right next to it — on the one control in the bar that has no fallback route if missed.
findings.fix: Give `.avatar` the same `::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:-2px}` treatment `.iconbtn` already has (or increase its own width/height to 44px), so its real hit area matches its sibling.

findings.title: First-run join/create inputs miss the Enter-to-submit handler their duplicate 'another board' inputs have
findings.where: index.html:5388-5391 (create-board input) and 5396-5400 (join-code input), vs. the near-identical 5576-5579 and 5592-5597
findings.detail: The zero-groups screen's 'Create your unit's board' name input (5388-5391) and 'Join with a code' input (5396-5400) have no `onKeyDown` handler. The visually and behaviorally identical inputs shown later once a nurse already has ≥1 group — 'Create another board' (5578-5579) and 'Join another board' (5595-5597) — both carry `onKeyDown={e=>{ if(e.key==='Enter') doCreateGroup(); }}` / `doJoinGroup()`. Same field, same button, same purpose; only the first-run copy lacks the keyboard submit path.
findings.failure: A nurse joining her unit's board for the very first time (the most common swap-board entry point: a colleague texted her a 6-char code rather than tapping a link) types the code one-handed with the iOS keyboard up, then has no keyboard-native way to submit — Return/Go does nothing here — so she has to dismiss or work around the keyboard to find and tap 'Join board' below. The exact same action a returning user takes to join a SECOND board works fine with Return, so the app is inconsistent about which keyboard behavior she gets on identical UI.
findings.fix: Add the same `onKeyDown={e=>{ if(e.key==='Enter') doJoinGroup(); }}` to the 5396-5400 input and `onKeyDown={e=>{ if(e.key==='Enter') doCreateGroup(); }}` to the 5388-5391 input, matching 5579/5597.

findings.title: Overtime tag text fails AA contrast in the Add-Shift live preview and shift list
findings.where: index.html:4197 and index.html:4245 (color '#11A86B' inline overrides; also the decorative badge at 3923 and legend swatch text-adjacent use at 4218 share the same token)
findings.detail: The 'OT ×1.5' annotation is rendered with inline color:'#11A86B' (var(--money)). At line 4197 it sits on the 'ON THIS DAY' row list's white background (.row-item{background:#fff}, line 421) — measured contrast 3.07:1. At line 4245 it sits on the live preview's mint-tinted panel (.preview{background:var(--money-soft)}, line 418) — measured contrast 2.75:1. Both are far under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for normal-weight text this size (12-12.5px, not 'large text' under WCAG's 14pt-bold/18pt threshold). The base take-home figures next to it use var(--money-ink) (#0B5D3C), which passes easily (7.1:1+) — only the OT accent color is broken.
findings.failure: A low-vision nurse comparing 'is this shift worth picking up because of the OT multiplier' sees a washed-out, hard-to-read 'OT ×1.5' tag right next to the dollar amount that explains why the number is higher than a normal shift — exactly the moment this app is built to make legible.
findings.fix: Swap the inline color:'#11A86B' for var(--money-ink) (#0B5D3C) in the OT tag at both call sites (and the calendar badge/legend for consistency) — it already passes AA against every background in use and matches the color already used for the adjacent dollar figures.

findings.title: Danger-red money text narrowly fails AA on the app's translucent glass panels
findings.where: index.html:3999 (Breakdown deduction rows, rendered inside the modal at 3620-3628), index.html:4571 (Pattern Lab 'will be replaced' warning inside .preview), index.html:4716/4755 (.danger-link 'Del' buttons in the Settings modal)
findings.detail: var(--danger) (#C84B3C) is used at 12-13px/600 weight for deduction values, warnings and 'Del' links. Computed against the literal token values: on the near-opaque .card background used when Breakdown is embedded inline (rgba(255,255,255,.93), line 111, call site 3586) it's ~4.64:1 — passes. But the same red text rendered inside .modal (rgba(246,245,241,.88) over the dark .scrim, lines 394/399) or .preview (var(--money-soft) #E3F7EE, line 418) computes to ~4.15-4.25:1 — under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text. That's the Breakdown popup (line 3625 'See the full breakdown'), the Settings goal/differential Del buttons, and the Pattern Lab apply-preview warning — three of the named money surfaces.
findings.failure: The same federal-tax/FICA/state-tax deduction figures are legible when shown inline on the dashboard but slip just under the AA contrast floor when the user taps 'See the full breakdown ›' to view them in the popup, because that surface's glass panel is measurably less opaque than the plain white card.
findings.fix: Either drop the .modal/.preview backdrop-filter tint under var(--danger) text specifically, or darken var(--danger) by a few percent so it clears 4.5:1 against #E3F7EE and the translucent panel's effective color, not just against pure white.

findings.title: Add-Shift and Pattern Lab live money readouts have no aria-live region
findings.where: index.html:4243-4249 (AddShiftSheet .preview block) and index.html:4539-4544 (.pl-money readout in Pattern Lab)
findings.detail: previewGross/previewNet (computed at 4104-4105) and metrics.periodNet/periodGross (patternMetrics) re-render live as the user toggles shift type, hours, OT, bonus, or paints pattern cells, but the containing divs carry no aria-live attribute. Elsewhere in the same file the team does wire this up correctly — the toaster (`role="status" aria-live="polite"`, line 2118) and the pay-period label (`aria-live="polite"`, line 3457) — so the omission here is inconsistent, not a deliberate choice.

findings.fix: Wrap the `.preview` value line (and the `.pl-money` .v/.s lines) in `aria-live="polite"` (a single region per sheet is enough — no need to make every keystroke chatty at the character level, just the settled preview text).

findings.title: Calendar grid has no grid semantics or row-based navigation for screen reader / keyboard users
findings.where: index.html:3938 (`<div className="grid">`) and the day-cell buttons built at 3915-3936
findings.detail: Each day is an independent `<button>` with a rich aria-label (dt.toDateString() + shift/take-home/OT/note info, lines 3916-3922) — that part is done well. But the container has no `role="grid"`/`role="row"`/`role="gridcell"` and there is no roving-tabindex or arrow-key handling; the weekday header row is `aria-hidden="true"` (line 3952) with no equivalent exposed elsewhere. Every day in the visible month(s) is one flat Tab stop in a single sequential order.
findings.failure: A keyboard or screen-reader user who wants to check the take-home for a date three weeks out must Tab through every single day between today and then one at a time — there is no 'next week' / row-jump the way a native `role="grid"` (arrow keys) would give them, and nothing announces that this region is even a calendar grid rather than an arbitrary list of buttons.
findings.fix: Wrap each week row in `role="row"`, mark cells `role="gridcell"` inside a `role="grid"` container (or, more simply, add a `role="grid"`/roving-tabindex layer per WAI-ARIA APG's grid pattern) so assistive tech can navigate by week/row instead of one cell at a time.

findings.title: Pay-period stepper's scroll animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion
findings.where: animateScrollTop (index.html:674-683), used by scrollFocusToDate (index.html:2751-2766) via movePeriod (index.html:2826-2831)
findings.detail: The ‹/› pay-period stepper in the greet row calls movePeriod, which calls scrollFocusToDate, which drives the calendar's scroll position with animateScrollTop — a hand-rolled requestAnimationFrame loop that eases el.scrollTop over 380ms. This is plain JS, not a CSS transition/animation. The file's own reduced-motion rule (index.html:469-471, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ *{animation-duration:.001ms!important;transition-duration:.001ms!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important} }`) only collapses CSS-driven durations and `scroll-behavior` (native smooth-scroll); it has no effect on a loop that sets `el.scrollTop` directly on every rAF frame. There is no `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` check anywhere in the file (confirmed via grep).
findings.failure: A user with 'reduce motion' enabled at the OS level taps › next to the pay-period label while in Month view. The entire calendar viewport still animates a smooth 380ms scroll to the new period's position — exactly the kind of scrolling motion the reduced-motion setting exists to suppress, and exactly the kind of thing this same file is careful to suppress for boot timers/CSS transitions elsewhere.
findings.fix: Check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` at the top of animateScrollTop (or in scrollFocusToDate before calling it) and jump `el.scrollTop = clamped` synchronously instead of animating when the user has that preference set.

findings.title: Month/Year view control uses role="tablist"/"tab" without the tab keyboard pattern
findings.where: index.html:3547-3550 (the .viewseg buttons)
findings.detail: The Month/Year toggle is marked up as `<div className="viewseg" role="tablist" aria-label="Calendar view">` wrapping two `role="tab" aria-selected={...}` buttons. Per the ARIA tab pattern this markup promises to a screen-reader/keyboard user: Left/Right arrow keys move selection between tabs, and each tab is wired to its panel via aria-controls (with a matching role="tabpanel"). Neither exists: there is no onKeyDown handler anywhere on these buttons or their container (confirmed — the only onKeyDown handlers in the whole file are on unrelated text inputs at lines 4035, 4281, 5357, 5579, 5597), and `aria-controls`/`role="tabpanel"` appear nowhere in the file.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user tabs to the control and hears "Month, tab, 1 of 2, selected" — the standard tab-pattern announcement — and, following that pattern, presses the Right arrow key expecting focus/selection to move to "Year". Nothing happens; they have to already know to abandon the arrow-key convention and Tab past it instead.
findings.fix: Either implement the real pattern (roving tabindex + arrow-key handler that calls setCalView, plus aria-controls pointing at a role="tabpanel" wrapping the YearList/cal-vscroll region), or drop role="tablist"/"tab"/aria-selected and let it be a plain labeled button group — a segmented control doesn't have to be ARIA tabs.

findings.title: Year-view prev/next buttons have a vague, ungrouped aria-label
findings.where: index.html:3553-3557 (.calnav div and its two buttons)
findings.detail: In Year view, the prior/next-year buttons are `aria-label="Previous"` and `aria-label="Next"` with no wrapping group label — contrast with the pay-period stepper right above it (index.html:3457), which wraps identical-looking ‹/› buttons in `role="group" aria-label="Pay period"` and gives the buttons themselves `aria-label="Previous pay period"`/`"Next pay period"`. The Year-view .calnav div has no role or aria-label at all.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user tabbing through the calendar card in Year view reaches a button announced only as "Previous, button" — nothing says it steps by year (versus the pay-period stepper's control, one screen away, which does say what it steps). They have to explore surrounding content to guess what it does.
findings.fix: Label the buttons `aria-label="Previous year"`/`"Next year"` (matching the pattern already used for the pay-period stepper), and/or add `role="group" aria-label="Year"` to the wrapping .calnav div.

findings.title: Day cell's "today" state is visual-only — dropped from the accessible name
findings.where: index.html:3913-3922 (Calendar function: isToday computed at 3913, cell button's aria-label built at 3916-3922)
findings.detail: `isToday` is computed and used only to add a CSS class (`(isToday?' today':'')` at 3916), which produces a 2px indigo inset ring via `.cell.today{box-shadow:...}` (index.html:244). Because the button carries an explicit aria-label, that manually-built string is its entire accessible name — and it is built from hasShift/hasEvent/take-home/hasOT/no-shifts/hasNote (3917-3922) but never from isToday. Every other visual-only day state that the aria-label author clearly cared about (overtime badge, note dot) IS mirrored into the label; "today" is the one omitted.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user navigating the day-cell buttons in Month view has no way to tell which one is today — sighted users get an indigo ring around it, but the announced label for that cell is indistinguishable from any other day with the same shifts/hours, e.g. "Fri Sep 12 2025, no shifts" reads identically whether or not it's actually today.
findings.fix: Append `(isToday ? ', today' : '')` to the aria-label string built at index.html:3916-3922.

findings.title: The month-scroll container isn't keyboard-scrollable on its own
findings.where: index.html:3561 (`<div className="cal-vscroll" ref={monthScrollRef} onScroll={onMonthScroll}>`)
findings.detail: `.cal-vscroll` is a nested `overflow-y:auto; max-height:60vh` scroll region (index.html:184) holding 16 months of day-cell buttons. It has no `tabIndex` and no keydown handler, so it is never itself a focus stop and never responds to arrow/Page keys. The outer page (`body`/document) is what actually scrolls when a keyboard-only user (no mouse/touch — e.g. a switch or keyboard-only sighted user, not necessarily a screen-reader user) presses Page Down/Space with focus elsewhere on the page; that scrolls the page around the calendar card, not the calendar's own internal 60vh viewport.
findings.failure: A sighted keyboard-only user wants to browse forward from the current month inside the calendar card without a pointer device. There is no key they can press with focus inside the calendar region to page the 60vh scroller itself — their only route is Tab-ing individually through every day-cell button in the current month (up to ~31 Tab presses) until focus-follows-into-view scrolls the next month into range, which works only as an incidental side effect of tabbing through unrelated buttons, not as an intentional "scroll the calendar" action.
findings.fix: Give `.cal-vscroll` `tabIndex={0}` (and ideally an `aria-label`, e.g. "Calendar months") so it becomes a standard scrollable region that responds to the browser's native arrow/Page/Home/End key scrolling once focused.

findings.where: index.html:4197 and index.html:4245 (AddShiftSheet)
findings.detail: Both the logged-shift row's 'OT ×1.5' tag (line 4197, on .row-item's #fff background) and the live preview's ' · incl. OT ×1.5' suffix (line 4245, on .preview's --money-soft #E3F7EE background) are colored with the literal '#11A86B' (the --money brand green), not the app's already-AA --money-ink (#0B5D3C) that every other dollar figure in the same sheet uses (e.g. .preview .v and .preview .k at CSS lines 419-420, and .cell .amt at 236). Computed contrast: #11A86B on #fff ≈ 3.07:1; #11A86B on #E3F7EE ≈ 2.75:1. Both text runs are 12-14px bold, well under the ≥18.66px-bold 'large text' exemption, so both need 4.5:1 and both fail.
findings.failure: A low-vision nurse (the app's stated audience) viewing a logged shift or the live preview for a shift she flagged as overtime can fail to read the 'OT ×1.5' qualifier at all, since it renders at roughly half the minimum required contrast right next to (and in the same weight as) the fully-legible dark-green take-home figures beside it.
findings.fix: Use var(--money-ink) (already proven AA-compliant at ~12:1+ on both backgrounds and used for every other dollar figure in this sheet) for the OT text instead of the literal '#11A86B'; keep '#11A86B' for non-text accents like the small dot indicators if desired.

findings.title: Add-Shift sheet has no dialog semantics, unlike every sibling sheet in the same file
findings.where: index.html:4164 (AddShiftSheet's outer <div className="sheet">)
findings.detail: Every other modal sheet in the app declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="..." on its .sheet element: the feedback sheet (line 2057, aria-label="Send feedback"), the .ics import-confirm sheet (3820, "Confirm schedule import"), the classify-imported-shift sheet (3848, "Classify imported shift"), and both swap sheets (5311/5330, "Shift swaps"). AddShiftSheet's own <div className="sheet"> at 4164 carries none of these. There is also no Escape-key handler anywhere for this sheet (the only keydown listener in the whole app is the account menu's, lines 1966-1968) or focus management on open/close.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user who opens 'Add a shift' from a calendar day gets no announcement that a dialog named 'Add a shift' just opened, and the assistive-tech virtual cursor is free to wander into the calendar/dashboard behind the scrim while it is nominally modal — the exact opposite of what happens one sheet over (Import/Classify/Feedback/Swaps) for the identical visual pattern. The same user also has no keyboard way to dismiss it (Escape does nothing here, though it works for the account menu).
findings.fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Add a shift" to the .sheet div at line 4164, matching the existing pattern, and give it the same document keydown Escape->dismiss() handling already implemented for the account menu (1966-1968).

findings.title: Every 'Remove' button for a logged shift shares the identical accessible name
findings.where: index.html:4200 (inside the list.map over `list` in AddShiftSheet)

The same component already knows how to disambiguate an equivalent case: the template-delete button a few dozen lines earlier is `aria-label={'Delete template '+t.name}`.

findings.fix: Give each Remove button a distinguishing aria-label, e.g. aria-label={'Remove '+(differentials[s.shiftType]?.name||s.shiftType)+' ×'+s.hours+'h shift'}, mirroring the 'Delete template '+t.name pattern already used in the same file.

findings.title: Pattern Lab's dialog has no dialog role, no aria-modal, and no accessible name — unlike every sibling sheet
findings.where: index.html:4417-4419 (list mode) and index.html:4486-4488 (edit mode), function PatternLab
findings.detail: PatternLab's outer markup is `<div className="scrim" onClick={dismiss}><div className="modal" onClick={e=>e.stopPropagation()}>...`. Neither the scrim nor the modal div carries `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, or an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. Every other overlay in the app that plays the same role does carry this: FeedbackSheet (`role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Send feedback"`, line 2057), the confirm dialog (`role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"`, line 2138), the ICS import confirm (line 3820) and classify-shift (line 3848) sheets, and SwapsSheet (lines 5311, 5330) all declare it. PatternLab is the odd one out even though it visually looks and behaves like the same kind of sheet.
findings.failure: A VoiceOver/NVDA/TalkBack user taps 'Patterns' in the topnav (openPatternLab, line 2933). No 'dialog' role is announced and no name is given for what just opened — the screen reader has no signal that a new modal context replaced the page, and (because there is no aria-modal) it does not treat the rest of the page as hidden, so rotor/browse-mode navigation can wander into the calendar and topnav that are still present in the accessibility tree underneath.
findings.fix: Add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` and an `aria-label` (e.g. "Pattern lab" / "Edit pattern") to the `.modal` div in both the list-mode and edit-mode returns, matching the convention already used by FeedbackSheet/SwapsSheet/the ICS sheets.

findings.title: Pattern Lab has no focus trap and no Escape-to-close, so keyboard focus leaks into the obscured app behind it
findings.where: index.html:4300-4581 (function PatternLab, no keydown handling or focus management anywhere in the component); index.html:2596-2600 (body-scroll lock is the only 'modal open' side effect); index.html:1966-1968 (Escape-to-close exists for the account menu, for contrast)
findings.detail: There is no `useEffect`/`addEventListener('keydown', ...)` and no ref-based focus trap anywhere in PatternLab (confirmed by reading lines 4300-4420 and grepping the whole component body). The app never uses `ReactDOM.createPortal` (grep returns nothing) and never sets `inert` or toggles `aria-hidden` on background content when a sheet opens — the only 'a modal is open' side effect anywhere in the app is `document.body.style.overflow='hidden'` at line 2598, which blocks page scroll but does nothing to the DOM's tab order or accessibility tree. Meanwhile the account menu two thousand lines earlier (lines 1966-1968) does register a document keydown listener that closes on Escape, showing the app knows how to do this and simply didn't do it here.
findings.failure: A keyboard user opens Pattern Lab, then presses Shift+Tab from the '×' Close button (aria-label="Close", line 4419) — focus moves backward into whatever topnav/calendar control precedes PatternLab in the DOM (e.g. the 'Patterns'/'Swaps'/'Settings' topnav links or a calendar day cell), all of which are still fully interactive but visually hidden under the `.scrim` overlay (`rgba(18,18,26,.55)` + blur, line 394). The user sees no focus indicator at all (it's under the overlay) and can activate a background control — e.g. re-triggering `openPatternLab` or opening Settings underneath the already-open Pattern Lab — while apparently still 'inside' Pattern Lab. Separately, pressing Escape while Pattern Lab is open does nothing at all; the only ways to close it are clicking the × button or clicking the scrim backdrop.
findings.fix: Give the modal a focus trap (cycle Tab/Shift+Tab within its own focusable elements) and move focus onto it when it opens (e.g. the close button or heading), restoring focus to the invoking control on close; add a `keydown` listener for `Escape` that calls `dismiss()`, matching the pattern already used for the account menu at line 1966.

findings.title: The 'Put it on the calendar' apply preview updates silently for screen-reader users
findings.where: index.html:4566-4572 (the `.preview` div inside PatternLab's apply flow); contrast with index.html:3457 (`aria-live="polite"` on the analogous pay-period label)
findings.detail:
`applyPlan` (a `useMemo` over `applyStart`, `applyWeeks`, `applyReplace`, defined at lines 4312-4314) drives a plain `
` at lines 4566-4572 that reports 'This adds N shift(s) · ', how many days were skipped, and how many will be replaced. Changing the Starting date input, the 'FOR' week-count buttons, or the Replace toggle recomputes this text, but the div carries no `aria-live` region. Elsewhere in the same file the app already uses `aria-live="polite"` for exactly this kind of 'a control changed and this readout updated' case (the pay-period `{periodLabel}` at line 3457).
findings.failure: A screen-reader user changes 'FOR' from 6 weeks to 12 weeks, or flips 'Replace shifts already on those days' on, expecting to hear the updated add/skip/replace counts the sighted preview shows immediately. Nothing is announced — they have to manually re-navigate to the preview div after every change to learn whether their pattern will now replace shifts or add fewer than expected, which is exactly the kind of consequential, silent state change AA's programmatic-status guidance (and the app's own precedent at line 3457) exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add `aria-live="polite"` (and ideally `aria-atomic="true"`) to the `.preview` div at line 4567 so the recomputed adds/skipped/replaced counts are announced whenever `applyStart`, `applyWeeks`, or `applyReplace` change.

findings.title: Onboarding step transitions never move focus and use no heading markup
findings.where: index.html:5704-5835 (all 5 obStep branches), goObStep index.html:2198-2201, exit-to-app at index.html:3081/3391/3412
findings.detail: Every step change in the wizard (welcome -> base-rate -> differentials -> taxes -> done, the back button, and the final exit into the main dashboard when setupComplete flips to true) is a full React remount of a different JSX subtree in the same container. None of the five branches use an <h1>-<h6> for its question/heading text ("What's your base hourly rate?", "How does your pay change by shift?", etc. are all plain <div className="q">), there is no ref.focus()/autoFocus placed on any heading or first control after a transition, and no aria-live region wraps the step content. grep -n "<h1\|<h2\|<h3\|<h4" confirms zero headings anywhere inside Onboarding().
findings.failure: A VoiceOver or NVDA user taps 'Get my estimate' (index.html:5729). The button they were focused on is unmounted and replaced by the base-rate step; the browser silently drops focus to <body> (or leaves it nowhere useful), and nothing is announced. The user hears nothing happen and has no heading to jump to with the AT's heading-navigation shortcut (H in NVDA/JAWS, rotor in VoiceOver) -- they must re-explore the whole page from the top to discover the new question exists. This repeats at every one of the 5 steps and again on the transition out of onboarding into the live app.
findings.fix: Give each step's question a real heading (e.g. <h1 className="q">), and on obStep change move focus to that heading (or the step's first control) via a ref + useEffect keyed on obStep. Same treatment for the setupComplete flip into the main app.

findings.title: 'ESTIMATED' tax-rate tag fails WCAG AA contrast
findings.where: index.html:328 (.tag.est rule), rendered at index.html:5796 and index.html:5798
findings.detail: .tag.est{color:#C2820A;background:#FDF3DD} at 10.5px/600-weight. Computed contrast of #C2820A on #FDF3DD is 2.93:1 -- well under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text (it doesn't even clear the 3:1 large-text bar, and 10.5px isn't large text anyway). This is the badge sitting directly on 'Federal income tax' and 'State tax' in the onboarding taxes step (obStep 3), the two rates that feed the projected take-home figure shown one step later.
findings.failure: A low-vision nurse using the taxes step at obStep 3 cannot read the word 'ESTIMATED' next to Federal/State tax -- it visually all but disappears against its own pill background, so she can't tell which of the pre-filled numbers are guesses she should check versus fixed values (FICA's .tag.auto pill, by contrast, passes at 4.75:1).
findings.fix: Darken #C2820A (or lighten the pill background) until contrast clears 4.5:1 -- e.g. swap to the same indigo-on-indigo-soft treatment already used for .tag.auto, or darken to roughly #8A5A05 on the existing #FDF3DD.

findings.title: Settings modal has no dialog semantics and its close button has no accessible name
findings.where: index.html:4694-4697 (Settings)
findings.detail: Settings renders as `<div className="scrim"><div className="modal">...<button className="back" onClick={onClose}>{Ic.x}</button>` with no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no aria-label/aria-labelledby on the modal, and the close button wraps only the bare Ic.x SVG (index.html:603, a <path> with no <title>, no aria-hidden) with zero text or aria-label. Every sibling sheet in the same file gets this right at the same call-site shape: FeedbackSheet (index.html:2057, 2059) has role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Send feedback" plus aria-label="Close" on its X button; SwapsSheet (index.html:5311, 5305) and the ICS import sheets (index.html:3820,3822 / 3848,3850) do the same. When they do reach the X button in the header, it announces only 'button' with no label, so they cannot tell it closes Settings; the only other way out is the 'Done' button at the very bottom of a long, multi-section scrolling sheet (goals, differentials, taxes, calendar sync), which they may never discover.

findings.title: Render-blocking boot scripts prevent any paint (even the splash) until 5 cross-origin CDN fetches resolve
findings.where: index.html:17-21 (script tags), index.html:487 (#splash), index.html:490-592 (boot watchdog)
findings.detail: The 5 CDN scripts (React, ReactDOM, Babel standalone, pdf.js, supabase-js) are classic <script src> tags in <head> with no async/defer, spanning 3 third-party origins (unpkg.com x2, cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net). Per HTML parsing rules the browser must fetch+execute all 5 sequentially before continuing to parse the rest of <head> (the ~460-line <style> block) and reach <body> — so neither the #splash placeholder nor the boot watchdog script (which starts the 8s timer) can run until all 5 have loaded or errored.
findings.failure: On a slow or filtered connection (e.g. locked-down hospital Wi-Fi) where one of these 3rd-party origins stalls, the user sees a fully blank white tab with zero feedback — no spinner, no watchdog message — for as long as that network fetch hangs, because the watchdog's own 8s clock cannot start counting until the parser reaches the boot <script> tag, which requires all 5 earlier blocking scripts to have already resolved.
findings.fix: Add a minimal inline watchdog/fallback at the very top of <head>, before the 5 CDN script tags, so a loading/stalled-connection fallback can appear independent of whether those specific network fetches ever complete; alternatively investigate defer + Babel-standalone's DOMContentLoaded auto-transform to unblock initial parsing.

findings.fix: Wrap MonthSection (and/or Calendar) in React.memo with useCallback-stabilized keyOf/statOf/onPick, or at minimum unmount/hide the calendar tree while an overlay sheet is open (e.g. gate the `.dash` block on `!showSettings && !sheetDate && ...` the same way the body-scroll-lock effect already tracks those flags) so unrelated modal edits can't touch it.

findings.title: monthSecRefs never evicts refs for months that scroll out of the window, leaking detached DOM and corrupting the scroll-follow's nearest-section search
findings.where: index.html:2672 (monthSecRefs), :3568 (secRef callback), :2715-2734 (focusRowDates), :2720 (filter(Boolean))
findings.detail: `monthSecRefs.current` (a plain object, :2672) is written only on mount: `secRef={el=>{ if(el) monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]=el; }}` (:3568). React calls a callback ref with `null` on unmount, but the `if(el)` guard means that branch is silently skipped — so when `monthWindow` (:2663) recenters around a new `calFocus` (Year-view month taps at :3559, repeated Today jumps at :2848-2853 from a different month, or scrollFocusToDate's setCalFocus at :2762-2764 when walking many pay periods forward via movePeriod), the months that fall out of the ±3/+12 window unmount their DOM but their entries are never deleted from `monthSecRefs.current`. `focusRowDates()` (:2715-2734), which runs on every scroll-settle in Month view (:2735-2748), reads `Object.values(monthSecRefs.current).filter(Boolean)` (:2720) — `filter(Boolean)` does not remove these, since a detached DOM node reference is still truthy. So the list this function iterates over grows for the lifetime of the session with every distinct month ever visited, not just the 16 currently mounted, and it never shrinks.
findings.failure: A nurse who browses several months via Year view over a session accumulates stale detached-DOM references that are retained for the life of the tab (can't be GC'd) and are re-scanned via getBoundingClientRect() on every scroll-settle; in the edge case where the focus line briefly falls outside every live section's rect (scrolling to the very top/bottom of the loaded range), the fallback distance calc (:2724-2726) can pick one of these zero-rect detached sections as "closest" (its collapsed (0,0) rect can read as nearer to the focus line than a real, merely-off-screen section), pulling `.cell[data-date]` values from a long-abandoned month and silently snapping the active/highlighted pay period (via setPPS at :2746) to a date the user isn't looking at.
findings.fix: Have the ref callback also clear on unmount (`el===null`), e.g. `secRef={el=>{ if(el) monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]=el; else delete monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]; }}`, or rebuild `monthSecRefs.current` from `monthWindow`'s current key set whenever it changes.

findings.title: Scrolling the calendar past a pay-period boundary fires a real Supabase write
findings.where: index.html:2735-2748 (onMonthScroll -> setPPS), 2291-2295 (serializeState includes payPeriodStart), 2453-2487 (debounced save effect, payPeriodStart is a dependency at line 2487, and the body at 2459-2479 saves unconditionally once hydrated with no check that anything besides the view state changed)
findings.detail: payPeriodStart is part of the persisted blob (serializeState) and is a dependency of the 500ms-debounced cloud-save effect. onMonthScroll (a scroll-settle handler on the month view) calls setPPS(ps) whenever the scroll-follow logic decides the visible row belongs to a different pay period (line 2746: `if(ps && ps!==payPeriodStart) setPPS(ps)`). That state change alone re-triggers the save effect, and the effect has no content-equality guard against what was last written (unlike the 15s poll's own normalize() check at 2550/2560) - it only checks blob size and hydration status before calling saveToSupabase. So a signed-in user who just scrolls the month calendar to look at a future/past period, with no edits at all, produces a real network upsert to user_data roughly once per period boundary crossed (throttled only by the 500ms debounce and the 180ms scroll-settle timer).
findings.failure: A nurse casually scrolling through several months on her phone (checking a coworker's request, planning ahead) causes a burst of Supabase writes and a flashing 'Syncing...' indicator (line 3442) purely from browsing, once per pay-period boundary she scrolls past - wasted battery/data and free-tier write volume for a pure read/navigation action, and it also bumps updated_at, which can make a second signed-in device's 15s poll believe a real edit just landed when only the view moved.
findings.fix: Either drop payPeriodStart from the debounced-save trigger (persist the viewed period separately, e.g. only on pagehide/sign-out, or fold it into an existing save rather than scheduling a new one), or apply the same normalize()-style content-equality check the poll already uses (comparing serialized data with payPeriodStart zeroed out) before calling saveToSupabase, so a save that would be byte-identical is skipped.

findings.fix: Move syncing/syncError into a small isolated component (or context) that renders only the status label, so toggling it doesn't re-render Calendar/MonthSection at all - or wrap Calendar and MonthSection in React.memo with stabilized props (useCallback for statOf/keyOf/onPick, memoized differentials/shifts references) so a sync-status-only render bails out before reaching the calendar cells. findings.title: pagehide/visibilitychange flush silently drops an edit when the best-effort save fails
findings.where: index.html:2489-2505 (flush), contrast with the debounced save effect's failure handling at index.html:2470-2479; saveToSupabase at index.html:1324-1344
findings.detail: The debounced save effect explicitly guards against a failed cloud write: when saveToSupabase(...) resolves null (it always resolves, never throws — see the catch at 1339-1343 and the error branch at 1337), the else branch at line 2478 calls writeBackup(user.id, dataToSave) so the edit survives locally under BACKUP_KEY. The separate `flush` handler registered for `pagehide`/`visibilitychange`→hidden (added specifically because '500ms debounce would otherwise drop it', per the comment at 2489) does not do this: its call chain is `saveToSupabase(...).then(ts=>{ if(ts){ ...clear backup... } })` — the `if(ts)` guard only handles the success path. When `ts` is null/falsy (network drop, RLS/Postgres error, or the fetch simply being torn down mid-flight as the page actually unloads), the `.then` body does nothing: no writeBackup call, no error surfaced.
findings.failure: Signed-in user edits a shift, then immediately backgrounds or closes the tab (the debounce hasn't fired yet, which is exactly the case this handler exists for) on a flaky connection. The pagehide-triggered save fails; because flush's failure branch is a no-op, the edit is written to BACKUP_KEY nowhere, never reaches Supabase, and — once the tab is actually gone — no longer exists in memory either. On the next load, hydrateFromCloud finds no newer backup and no newer cloud row, so the edit is gone with no toast, no syncError, and no recovery path, unlike every other save-failure path in the app.
findings.fix: Mirror the debounced effect's failure handling in flush: when saveToSupabase resolves falsy, call writeBackup(snap.user.id, snap.data) just like line 2478 does. Because a `.then()` callback isn't guaranteed to run once actual page teardown begins, prefer writing the backup synchronously before firing the best-effort save (optimistic backup, cleared only on confirmed success) rather than only in the async continuation.

findings.title: An open Add-Shift sheet's stale in-memory draft can silently overwrite a same-day edit just pulled from another device
findings.where: AddShiftSheet's list/events/note state is captured once at mount from props (index.html:4076, 4083-4084) and never resynced; saveDayShifts unconditionally overwrites shifts[dateKey]/dayEvents[dateKey]/notes[dateKey] with that draft (index.html:2857-2874); the cross-device poll can apply a newer remote blob into the same state at any time the sheet is open (applyData at 2317/2325-2326 via the 15s interval, focus, and visibilitychange refetch at index.html:2547-2574)
findings.detail: AddShiftSheet is only mounted/unmounted on `sheetDate` null↔value transitions (index.html:3613-3618: `{sheetDate && <AddShiftSheet .../>}`, no `key` prop keying it to the date), so while it stays open its `list`/`events`/`note` state — seeded once from `existing`/`existingEvents`/`existingNote` at mount — never re-reads the `shifts`/`dayEvents`/`notes` props even if they change underneath it. But those props DO change underneath it: the cross-device refetch (2547-2574) fires on the 15s interval and immediately on `focus`/visible-`visibilitychange`, and on a content difference calls `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})`, which does a plain `setShifts(d.shifts)`/`setDayEvents(d.dayEvents)`/`setNotes(d.notes)` (2317, 2325-2326) — a full replace, not a per-day merge. When the sheet is later saved or dismissed-with-dirty-state, `saveDayShifts` (2857-2858) does `n[dateKey]=arr` (or the dayEvents/notes equivalents at 2867/2873) against whatever `prev` currently is, but `arr`/`events`/`note` are still the sheet's original stale draft.
findings.failure: Nurse signs into the same account on two devices. On device A she opens the Add-Shift sheet for a day and gets interrupted — she switches apps/tabs (backgrounding triggers no refetch, but returning fires an immediate `visibilitychange`/`focus` refetch). Meanwhile on device B she (or someone else with the login) added a shift to that same day; that write is now the newer cloud row. When she returns to device A, the refetch pulls device B's shift for that day into `shifts` — but the still-open sheet's `list` doesn't include it. She finishes her edit on device A and hits Save: `saveDayShifts` writes only her stale `list` for that date, so device B's just-synced shift for that day is silently discarded, then propagated to the cloud 500ms later with no conflict warning.
findings.fix: When shifts/dayEvents/notes for the currently-open `dateKey` change while the sheet is mounted, either re-seed the sheet's local draft (e.g. a useEffect keyed on the incoming day's content that merges or warns instead of overwriting) or have the cross-device refetch skip applying changes to a day that has an open, dirty sheet and re-check once it closes.

findings.title: 15s cross-device refetch can silently discard an edit that hasn't finished its 500ms debounce/network round-trip
findings.where: index.html:2547-2574 (poll/refetch effect), specifically the guard at 2557 and the applyData call at 2561; interacts with the debounced save at 2453-2487 (500ms timer at 2485)
findings.detail: The comment at index.html:2540-2543 claims the poll is 'guarded by updated_at AND content-equality so we never ... clobber unsaved local edits.' In fact `normalize()` (2550) only prevents re-applying byte-identical content (guards against echoing an already-synced row). It has no way to detect 'this device has a local edit that is still sitting in its 500ms debounce timer, or whose saveToSupabase call is still in flight, and hasn't reached the cloud yet.' `refetch()` only checks `hydratedForUser.current===user.id` (2553) before calling `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})` (2561) whenever `row.updatedAt` is newer than `lastSeenAt.current` and the fetched content differs from the current in-memory serialization — which it necessarily will differ whenever there is a pending, not-yet-saved local edit, since that edit by definition isn't reflected in either the fetched row or (yet) anywhere durable.
findings.failure: Same account signed in on two devices/tabs, A and B, both hydrated and in sync (lastSeenAt equal). Device A edits something (e.g. adds a shift) and its save completes, advancing the cloud row's updated_at. Moments later Device B makes an unrelated edit (e.g. corrects the base rate) — B's own 500ms debounce timer starts, and the network round-trip to Supabase hasn't completed yet. If B's `setInterval(refetch,15000)` tick, or a `focus`/`visibilitychange` event (2568-2571), fires during that window, `refetch()` sees A's newer `updated_at`, sees the fetched content differs from B's current state (because it doesn't yet include B's edit, which never reached the cloud), and calls `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})` — replacing ALL of B's in-memory state, including the edit just made, with A's snapshot. There is no merge, no conflict warning, and no backup: `writeBackup` (2273-2274) is invoked only when a cloud save FAILS, never when a remote refetch overwrites in-memory state. B's edit is gone with no indication anything happened, and B's own still-pending debounced save (now reflecting the reverted state) will shortly re-persist that reverted state to the cloud.
findings.fix: Before applying a remote row in `refetch()`, check whether a local save is currently pending or in flight (e.g. track a `saveInFlight`/`pendingLocalEdit` ref set when the debounce timer is armed or `saveToSupabase` is awaited, cleared once the write lands) and skip/defer the apply — or queue the refetched row and re-check content-equality once the pending local save resolves — instead of unconditionally overwriting state whenever content differs from the last-seen snapshot.

findings.title: Stale .ics import plan can resurrect a shift another device deleted, or clobber a concurrent edit, and the result gets persisted to the cloud
findings.where: index.html:3147-3191 (icsConfirmImport), 3089-3105 (buildIcsImportPlan closes over live `shifts`/`dayEvents`), 1511-1543 (icsPlanFromExisting captures shiftType/bonusType/hours at plan-build time), 2547-2574 (15s cross-device poll calls applyData which does a full setShifts(d.shifts) overwrite)
findings.detail: The .ics import/sync merge plan (`toUpdate`, with `prevShiftId`/`shiftType`/`bonusType`/`hours` frozen into `icsImport` state) is built once, from whatever `shifts`/`dayEvents` happened to be in scope at parse time (a manual file import, or `runIcalSync`'s up-to-12s proxy fetch). The user then reviews a multi-step questionnaire before tapping Confirm — this can take anywhere from seconds to a minute or more for several shift groups. During that whole window the independent cross-device sync poll (index.html:2547-2574) keeps running every 15s while the tab is visible, and on finding a newer cloud row calls `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})`, which does an unconditional `setShifts(d.shifts)` (index.html:2317) — a full state replacement, not a merge. When the user finally taps Confirm, `icsConfirmImport`'s `setShifts(prev=>...)` (3163) operates on whatever `prev` is *now* (post-poll), but for every `toUpdate` entry it unconditionally does `dropShift(u.prevDateKey,u.prevShiftId)` (no-op if that id is already gone) and then unconditionally re-inserts `{id:u.prevShiftId, shiftType:u.shiftType, hours:u.hours, ...}` (3171-3176) using the values captured at plan-build time — with no check that the shift still exists, is still at the state the plan assumed, or wasn't intentionally deleted/edited elsewhere in the meantime.
findings.failure: Nurse has BadgeBudget open on her phone and signed in on a tablet too (the app's advertised two-device use case). On the phone she opens Settings and taps 'Sync now' (or the silent app-open auto-sync fires and finds something to confirm), which opens the import questionnaire with several shift groups to classify. While she's still working through the cards, she deletes a shift on the tablet (it got cancelled) and it saves to the cloud. Within 15s the phone's background poll pulls that newer blob and removes the shift from `shifts` there too. She finishes the questionnaire on the phone and taps Confirm: `icsConfirmImport`'s stale `toUpdate` entry for that same icsUid re-adds the shift she just deleted on the tablet, with its old id/date/hours/pay type. The debounced save effect (2453-2487) then pushes this reconstituted shift back to Supabase, overwriting — permanently, last-writer-wins — the deletion she made on the other device. The same mechanism also silently reverts a pay-type/hours edit made on the other device mid-sync, since the plan's `shiftType`/`bonusType`/`hours` were snapshotted before that edit landed.
findings.fix: Re-derive (or at least re-validate) the merge plan against the current `shifts`/`dayEvents` at Confirm time rather than trusting the snapshot captured when the sheet opened — e.g. re-run `buildIcsImportPlan` (or just check that `u.prevShiftId` still exists at `u.prevDateKey` with the same fields) inside the `setShifts` functional updater, and drop/re-warn on any `toUpdate`/`toRemove` entry whose target shift already vanished or changed for a reason other than this sync.

findings.title: A shift that moved outside the 60-day-back/366-day-forward sync window is indistinguishable from a deleted shift, and the confirm screen states it as certain
findings.where: index.html:1545-1576 (icsPlanFromExisting removal logic, esp. `if(!inWindow(rec.dateKey)) return;`), 826-864 (parseICSSchedule drops out-of-window events before the caller ever sees them), 3828-3834 (IcsImportSheet: "Removing … — gone from your calendar feed.")
findings.detail: `parseICSSchedule` silently drops any VEVENT outside [today-60d, today+366d] (`droppedWindow`, 864) — the caller never learns the event still exists at a new date outside that range. `icsPlanFromExisting`'s removal pass then treats "this icsUid wasn't seen in the fresh parse" as "deleted from the calendar" as long as the *previously stored* dateKey is inside the window (1558-1566) — it has no way to tell "deleted" apart from "moved to a date the current fetch window doesn't cover." The confirm sheet then asserts, unconditionally, that the listed shifts are "gone from your calendar feed" (3832-3834) with no hedge.
findings.failure: A shift that was correctly imported near-term gets rescheduled in the source calendar to more than 366 days out (e.g. a hospital or travel-nurse contract that publishes far-future dates) or corrected to a date more than 60 days in the past. The next sync no longer sees that UID in-window, proposes it under "Removing … gone from your calendar feed," and if the user (trusting the app's own confident wording) taps Confirm, `icsConfirmImport` permanently deletes a shift that was never actually cancelled — losing real logged hours/pay-type data with no undo.
findings.fix: Either widen/soften the removal claim when the shift's own recorded date is near a window boundary, or track that the UID was seen previously and simply skip removal (leave it stored, unflagged) when its own current window straddles a boundary, and change the confirm copy from an assertion ("gone from your calendar feed") to a hedge (e.g. "no longer appears in the synced window").

findings.title: Whole-blob upsert has no compare-and-swap: a delayed/flaky-network write can silently roll back a newer, already-"saved" edit from another device, with no backup to recover it
findings.where: saveToSupabase() index.html:1324-1344; sync poll ordering check index.html:2551-2564; MAX_BLOB_BYTES/backup guard index.html:2454-2487
findings.detail: saveToSupabase() computes `updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` on the CLIENT before the network call, then does `.upsert({user_id, data, updated_at}, {onConflict:'user_id'})` with no WHERE/version guard (confirmed: no trigger or check constraint on user_data.updated_at in supabase/migrations/000_core.sql — it's a plain `default now()` column, never conditioned on in the upsert). Whichever request physically reaches Postgres LAST wins outright and overwrites both `data` and `updated_at`, regardless of which edit happened later in real time or what timestamp value it carries. The client-side ordering guard at index.html:2557 (`row.updatedAt > lastSeenAt.current`) only protects the LOCAL in-memory comparison on the polling device; it does nothing to stop the DB row itself from being overwritten by an out-of-order or clock-skewed write from another device.
findings.failure: Nurse edits a shift on her phone at a hospital with spotty WiFi (edit at real time T0); the save request is delayed in flight. Seconds later she edits the same data on her laptop at home over a good connection (edit at T1>T0); that save completes immediately and succeeds — clearing the laptop's own local backup (index.html:2475) because its save succeeded. If the phone's delayed request then arrives at Supabase after the laptop's, the row is overwritten with the phone's STALE data and an OLDER `updated_at`. The laptop's newer edits are now gone from the cloud. Because they were never in `writeBackup()` (that only fires when a save FAILS, and the laptop's save reported success), there is no copy anywhere to recover them once the laptop's tab is closed or its browser data cleared — reopening the app anywhere else (or signing in on a new device) hydrates the phone's older data. The laptop's own 15s poll never flags this either, because the phone's `updated_at` is chronologically earlier than the laptop's `lastSeenAt`, so `row.updatedAt > lastSeenAt.current` is false and the discrepancy is never even surfaced.
findings.fix: Add an optimistic-concurrency guard to the upsert (e.g. pass the last-seen `updated_at` and use `.eq('updated_at', lastSeenAt)` with an update, falling back to insert/upsert only when no row exists yet), or move to a monotonic version column with a DB-side check so a stale write is rejected (surfacing a conflict to the user/backup path) instead of silently winning. This does not require full versioned ops (PR #67's scope) — just enough to stop a slower write from clobbering a faster one.

findings.title: differentials is the one user-growable collection in sanitizeData with no cap, so it alone can push the blob past MAX_BLOB_BYTES and freeze cloud sync with no cross-device recovery
findings.where: sanitizeData differentials branch index.html:1041-1050 (no slice/cap, contrast with goals at 1072-1082 and MAX_GOALS at 634); addDiff() index.html:4692 (unconditional push, no length check unlike the goals-add path at 4685)
findings.detail: Every other user-appendable collection is capped both in the UI and in sanitizeData: goals (MAX_GOALS=12, enforced at index.html:4685 and sliced at 1076), templates (MAX_TEMPLATES, sliced at 1058), patterns (MAX_PATTERNS=8, sliced at 1093), dayEvents (MAX_DAY_EVENTS per day, sliced at 1006). `differentials` has neither: `addDiff()` at 4692 unconditionally adds a new `custom-<timestamp>` key with no length check, and sanitizeData's differentials block (1041-1050) validates each entry's shape but never slices or caps the count.
findings.failure: A user who keeps adding custom differentials (e.g. one per unit/role variant she works) eventually pushes the serialized blob past MAX_BLOB_BYTES (512KB). At that point the save effect's guard at index.html:2464-2469 returns BEFORE calling saveToSupabase at all — the cloud row freezes at whatever it held before the last differential that tipped it over, and the toast fires once (`oversizeWarned.current`) and is easy to dismiss/miss. If she then signs in on a second device, hydrateFromCloud pulls that frozen, now-stale cloud row: the differentials she added after crossing the cap are missing there, with the only copy sitting in the first device's `writeBackup()` local mirror.
findings.fix: Add a MAX_DIFFERENTIALS cap enforced both in addDiff() and as a `.slice(0, MAX_DIFFERENTIALS)` in sanitizeData's differentials branch, matching the pattern already used for goals/templates/patterns/dayEvents.

findings.title: handleSignOut doesn't clear the iCal feed URL/subscription state its own comment says it mirrors
findings.where: index.html:2528-2538 (handleSignOut) vs index.html:2409-2419 (onAuthStateChange SIGNED_OUT branch)
findings.detail: The SIGNED_OUT branch of onAuthStateChange (2409-2419) resets `hydratedForUser.current`, `setSyncError(false)`, `resetToDefaults()`, `lastSeenAt.current`, and ALSO `setHydratedUserId(null); setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl(''); icalSyncedForUser.current = null;`. handleSignOut (2528-2538) resets `hydratedForUser.current`, `lastSeenAt.current`, `prevUserId.current`, `setSyncError(false)`, `setSession(null)`, `setUser(null)`, `resetToDefaults()` — but never touches `icalSub`/`icalUrl`/`hydratedUserId`/`icalSyncedForUser`. `resetToDefaults()` itself (2335-2340) also doesn't touch them; that state lives only in the two places above. The comment at 2531-2532 explicitly claims handleSignOut 'Mirrors the SIGNED_OUT branch (safe/idempotent if that also fires)' — but the two lists have already drifted; handleSignOut is missing a quarter of what it claims to mirror.
findings.failure: signOutClient (2523-2527) exists specifically because supabase-js's own signOut() can deadlock on iOS WebKit — the same bug the getSession 4s-race guards, per the comment at 2518-2521, which also says 'Force signed-out state locally — never rely on onAuthStateChange, which won't fire if signOut stalled.' So on an iPhone where the underlying signOut() call actually stalls (the exact scenario this code was written for), onAuthStateChange's SIGNED_OUT branch — the only place icalSub/icalUrl/hydratedUserId get cleared — never runs. The user taps 'Sign out', confirms the dialog, and the UI shows them signed out (session/user cleared, dashboard resets), but the Settings sheet's calendar-sync input is still bound to `icalUrl` (index.html:4790, `value={icalUrl}`) and keeps rendering the PREVIOUS account's secret iCal feed URL — Invariant 13's bearer credential — in a plain-text field, along with `icalSub.lastSynced` (4800-4801), until a fresh sign-in overwrites that state. On a shared or handed-down device this exposes another nurse's private calendar address to whoever opens Settings next.
findings.fix: Add the same four lines (`setHydratedUserId(null); setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl(''); icalSyncedForUser.current = null;`) to handleSignOut, or factor the shared cleanup (used identically at 2409-2417 and needed at 2533-2536) into one function called from both sites so they can't drift apart again.

findings.title: ficaWithholdingType is passed through sanitizeData with no allowlist, so an unrecognized value silently zeroes FICA in computeNet
findings.where: index.html:963 (sanitizeData) and index.html:1237-1239 (computeNet)
findings.detail: sanitizeData's job, per its own header comment (index.html:948-952), is to keep a malformed blob from 'silently corrupt[ing] every calculation with string/NaN fields.' Every other enum-like wage field it handles is allowlisted with a safe fallback: estimateMode only ever lands on '' (line 969, with an explicit comment about being 'whitelisted, so a corrupt or hostile blob can only ever land on nothing'), differentials[k].type falls back to 'dollar' if it isn't one of the three valid values (line 1047), customWithholdings[].type is required to be 'percent'|'dollar' or the whole entry is dropped (line 1035). ficaWithholdingType gets none of that: line 963 is `if(typeof d.ficaWithholdingType==='string') out.ficaWithholdingType = d.ficaWithholdingType;` — any string at all passes through untouched. computeNet then only recognizes exactly 'standard' or 'percent' (lines 1238-1239); `let fica = 0` at 1237 is never reassigned for any other value, including a typo'd case, a stale/renamed option from a future revert, a hand-edited export, or corrupted localStorage/cloud data.
findings.failure: A user_data blob (or localStorage/imported-JSON blob) with ficaWithholdingType set to anything other than the exact strings 'standard' or 'percent' — e.g. 'Standard', an old/removed option name, or simple corruption — passes sanitizeData unchanged (line 963) and is applied via applyData's `if(d.ficaWithholdingType) setFicaType(d.ficaWithholdingType)` (line 2311) with no validation there either. Every subsequent computeNet() call (the hero figure, the Breakdown 'FICA' row, patternMetrics) then silently computes fica=0. For a nurse grossing $2,400 in a pay period that's roughly $184 (7.65%) of overstated take-home shown with no error, no banner, and no indication anything is wrong — exactly the class of bug sanitizeData's own header comment says it exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Allowlist ficaWithholdingType in sanitizeData the same way estimateMode and the differential/withholding `type` fields are handled: `out.ficaWithholdingType = (d.ficaWithholdingType==='standard'||d.ficaWithholdingType==='percent') ? d.ficaWithholdingType : 'standard';` (or omit the key entirely on an invalid value so applyData's own current value is kept). This is an Invariant 3 change — needs the wage-core protocol (baseline probes, a new assertion, and the hero/breakdown equality check against the deployed build).

findings.title: PTO gross/hours formula is copy-pasted in three places instead of two of them calling the existing ptoStatOf helper
findings.where: index.html:2636-2641 (ptoStatOf), index.html:2801-2806 (calc), index.html:2777 (yearMonths)
findings.detail: ptoStatOf (2636-2641) already encapsulates 'for each PTO day-event with hours>0, add hours*baseRate to gross and hours to total' and is the function statOf (2644-2650) correctly delegates to. calc() (2801-2806) and yearMonths (2777) reimplement the identical `if(e.kind==='pto' && e.hours>0){ gross/g += e.hours*baseRate; hours/h += e.hours; }` inline instead of calling ptoStatOf(k) per date key, even though both already iterate dayEvents by key exactly the way ptoStatOf expects.
findings.failure: PTO pricing currently has no cap and pays base rate for any hours>0 entered, but that's an easy invariant to want to change (e.g. capping paid PTO at 8h/day, or taxing PTO at a different rate than worked time — both plausible nightly-loop-sized feature requests given the BACKLOG's granularity). A dev following the wage-core protocol would naturally edit ptoStatOf (the function whose name says 'PTO stat') and verify the day-cell/calendar figures it feeds, but calc() (the pay-period hero/Breakdown total) and yearMonths (the Year view total) would keep the old formula unless the dev also remembers those two separate inline copies — so the hero's 'PTO adds to gross' figure or the Year view total would silently disagree with what the calendar cells show for the same PTO day.
findings.fix: Have calc() and yearMonths call ptoStatOf(k) (or a shared pure helper it wraps) instead of re-deriving the same two-line PTO formula, so there is exactly one place that defines 'what a PTO day is worth.'

findings.title: sampleNet() (onboarding's projected take-home) hand-rolls the same tax formula as computeNet() instead of calling it, and isn't part of the Invariant 3 function list
findings.where: index.html:3416-3423 (sampleNet, inside applyPaystub's App scope) vs index.html:1231-1251 (computeNet)
findings.detail: sampleNet builds a 6-shift sample, sums shiftGross correctly, but then reimplements FICA-base/income-tax-base/fed/state/net entirely by hand (3419-3422) instead of calling `computeNet(g, taxInputs)` the way calc() (line 2809) and patternMetrics() (line 1298) do. It also never includes customWithholdings (`cw` in computeNet, lines 1242-1243) at all — every other real net calculation in the app sums customWithholdings into deductions; this one doesn't. sampleNet is not named anywhere in Invariant 3's protected function list (shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet/calc/statOf/ptoStatOf/patternMetrics), so the wage-core skill's required baseline probes and 'equality assertion against the deployed build' never exercise it.
findings.failure: This is the literal dollar figure shown on the 'You're all set' onboarding screen (line 5822, 'Projected take-home'), a nurse's very first number from the app. If a future wage-core change alters computeNet's formula (e.g. how FICA or a deduction cap works) and is verified correctly per the wage-core protocol, sampleNet's independent copy is not in scope for that verification and can silently diverge — the onboarding preview would show a different take-home than the hero/Breakdown will show moments later for an equivalent shift mix. Concretely today: any state where customWithholdings is non-empty (reachable via the supported Export JSON → hand-edit → Import JSON round trip, since sanitizeData validates and computeNet already sums that array) makes sampleNet's net figure too high by exactly the omitted withholding amount, while calc()/Breakdown correctly subtract it.
findings.fix: Replace sampleNet's inline tax math with `computeNet(g, {pretaxDeductions,posttaxDeductions,ficaType,ficaPct,federalTaxRate,stateTaxRate,customWithholdings})` (or reuse the existing `taxInputs` memo shape) so onboarding's preview and the real hero can never drift, and add it to the wage-core protocol's coverage.

findings.title: Per-day/period money rollup (shifts + PTO) hand-duplicated in 3 places instead of calling statOf/ptoStatOf
findings.where: index.html:2636-2650 (ptoStatOf/statOf) vs 2775-2777 (yearMonths) vs 2793-2805 (calc)
findings.detail: ptoStatOf+statOf is the one place that is supposed to define 'a day's money': shiftGross summed over shifts[k], plus PTO at `e.hours*baseRate` for dayEvents[k]. yearMonths (year-view totals) and calc (the hero figure, via taxInputs/computeNet) don't call statOf/ptoStatOf — each re-implements the identical two loops (`shifts[k].forEach(s=>{g+=shiftGross(...);h+=s.hours})` and `if(e.kind==='pto'&&e.hours>0){g+=e.hours*baseRate;h+=e.hours}`) inline. The comment at 2776 ('PTO adds to gross/hours like every other rollup (statOf/calc)') itself acknowledges the parallel implementations exist rather than being shared.
findings.failure: A future change to how PTO is priced (e.g. paying PTO at a shift's differential rate instead of flat baseRate, or capping PTO hours) is a plausible ask and touches statOf/ptoStatOf, whose output feeds the calendar day cells. If the dev updates statOf/ptoStatOf only (they're the named, documented rollup) and the harness's calendar assertions pass, the hero figure (calc, 2793-2805) and the Year view totals (yearMonths, 2768-2780) keep computing PTO the old way — a nurse would see the calendar day cell disagree with the hero total for the same pay period, with nothing in the diff or the existing tests catching it because there is no single function all three call.
findings.fix: Have calc() and yearMonths() call statOf(k)/ptoStatOf(k) (or a shared pure helper both can use outside the per-day closure) instead of re-summing shifts/dayEvents inline, so PTO/shift pricing has exactly one implementation.

findings.title: Onboarding's 'Projected take-home' preview reimplements computeNet's tax formula instead of calling it
findings.where: index.html:3416-3421 (sampleNet) vs 1231-1251 (computeNet)
findings.detail: sampleNet() — which drives the money figure on onboarding step 4 ('Based on a typical two-week schedule, here's what you'd take home', styled like the hero) — hand-computes FICA/federal/state/net from baseRate/differentials/ficaType/ficaPct/federalTaxRate/stateTaxRate/pretaxDeductions/posttaxDeductions instead of calling computeNet(gross, taxInputs) the way calc() (2807) and patternMetrics() (1298) do. It currently matches computeNet's arithmetic for the standard/percent FICA cases (customWithholdings don't exist in onboarding state, so that term is moot), but it's a second hand-written copy of the tax model with no shared code path.
findings.failure: Invariant 3's protocol for changing computeNet requires wage-math probes plus a hero/breakdown equality assertion against the deployed build — none of that touches sampleNet, since it isn't computeNet. A future correction to the tax model (e.g. a FICA/deduction-base bugfix) done correctly under that protocol would leave this onboarding screen silently showing the old, now-wrong number, with no test noticing because sampleNet is a textually separate formula.
findings.fix: Replace the inline arithmetic in sampleNet with `computeNet(g, {ficaType, ficaPct, federalTaxRate, stateTaxRate, pretaxDeductions, posttaxDeductions})` and read `.net` from the result.

findings.title: Day-key stringification is independently reimplemented three times over the same shifts/dayEvents object
findings.where: index.html:658 (keyOfDate), index.html:837 (keyOfYMD), index.html:2623 (App's local keyOf)
findings.detail: There are three separately-declared, currently byte-identical implementations of "format a Date/y-m-d as the calendar's 'YYYY-MM-DD' key": module-level `keyOfDate` (line 658, used by pattern-lab's planPatternApply at 1313/1318 and the sample-shift seed at 711, whose output is written straight into `shifts[k]`/`dayEvents[k]` via applyPattern's `next[k]=...` at 2960-2967), the ics-import parser's local `keyOfYMD` (line 837, used to build every imported shift/event's `dateKey`, which is written into the same `shifts`/`dayEvents` state via `next[u.dateKey]=...` at line 3175/3187), and App's own local `keyOf` (line 2623), which every calendar-facing read (Calendar/MonthSection cell lookup `shifts[keyOf(dt)]` at 3891/3907, `calc`'s period scoping at 2791, `yearMonths`' month-prefix scan at 2769-2780, `saveDayShifts`, `movePeriod`, `openSheetForLog`) goes through. None of these three functions references any of the others — they are copy-pasted text, not a shared symbol.
findings.failure: Any future change to the day-key format (e.g. guarding against a bad ics DTSTART, or fixing a locale/padding edge case) that is applied to only one of the three copies — which is easy, since grepping for `keyOfDate(` or `keyOf(` will not surface the other two definitions — makes that code path emit keys in a different string shape than the other two producers/consumers use. Concretely: if `keyOfYMD` (ics import) were ever patched without also patching `keyOf` (the calendar's own lookup function), an imported shift would be written under e.g. `shifts['2026-9-5']` while the calendar grid, `calc`, and `yearMonths` all look it up as `shifts['2026-09-05']||[]` — the shift would silently vanish from the calendar and the take-home totals (no error, just an empty array from the mismatched key), even though the ics import itself reported success.
findings.fix: Delete App's local `keyOf` and the ics parser's local `keyOfYMD`; have both call the single module-level `keyOfDate` (wrapping the y/mo/d ics case as `keyOfDate(new Date(y, mo-1, d))`). One function, one place to fix a date-key bug, and every consumer picks up the fix automatically.

findings.title: Month-section ref map never clears entries on unmount, so the pay-period stepper can silently stop scrolling the calendar
findings.where: index.html:3568 (secRef callback), consequence at index.html:2762-2765 (scrollFocusToDate) and index.html:2720 (focusRowDates), comment at index.html:2707-2713
findings.detail: `secRef={el=>{ if(el) monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]=el; }}` (line 3568) only ever sets an entry; it ignores the `null` React passes to a callback ref when the element unmounts, so it never deletes the entry. `monthWindow` (2663-2670) is a sliding 16-month window (`MONTH_BEFORE=3`/`MONTH_AFTER=12`, line 2662) around `calFocus`, so as the user browses to distant months (Year view, or repeated `movePeriod`/stepper taps) and back, months that scroll out of the window unmount their `MonthSection`, but `monthSecRefs.current[thatKey]` keeps pointing at the now-detached DOM node forever. `scrollFocusToDate` (2751-2766), used by the greet-row pay-period stepper `movePeriod` (2826-2831), decides whether to remount the target month purely from `if(!monthSecRefs.current[dateISO.slice(0,7)])` truthiness — a stale-but-truthy entry makes it take the `else align()` branch and skip `setCalFocus` entirely.
findings.failure: Browse far enough from the current month that it drops out of the live 16-month window (e.g. open Year view and jump to a year switched away from, or step `movePeriod` past it), so that month's MonthSection unmounts while its stale ref lingers; then step the pay-period `‹`/`›` control (or otherwise call `movePeriod`) back to a period whose start falls in that previously-visited month. `setPPS(newStart)` still runs, so the hero/breakdown figures switch to the new period, but `scrollFocusToDate` sees the stale truthy ref, never calls `setCalFocus`, `container.querySelector('.cell[data-date=...]')` finds nothing (the real DOM was actually removed), and `align()` no-ops — the visible scrolling calendar stays parked on unrelated months while the rest of the UI has already moved to the new pay period.
findings.fix: Give the callback ref an else-branch that deletes the stale entry: `secRef={el=>{ if(el) monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]=el; else delete monthSecRefs.current[mo.key]; }}`, matching the standard React callback-ref contract and keeping `monthSecRefs.current` bounded to the currently-mounted window — which is also what the `focusRowDates` comment already assumes (">=16 cheap rect reads", line 2710) but the code no longer guarantees.
